requirements.statement: A tenant administrator must be able to manage users, roles, spaces, connections, model endpoints, workflow definitions, style catalogues, vocabularies and retention policies
Every administrative action must be audited (**LIF-026**)
Administration must be reachable through the API on the same terms as the interface (**API-004**)
A destructive administrative action must state what it will affect before it is confirmed
Configuration must be exportable and importable, so that a tenant can be reproduced (**IMP-018**)

A configuration export must carry a reference to each secret rather than its value, and an import must bind every reference to a secret in the receiving tenant. An import with an unbound reference must be refused, naming each one (ADM-005, ADM-008, **IMP-018**)
A tenant administrator must be able to read and search their own tenant's audit log, filtered by actor, action, date and artifact, without raising a support ticket
A tenant administrator must be able to export their own tenant's audit log, complete rather than a page of results (**LIF-028**), scoped to that tenant alone

Scheduled and system work that affects a tenant - a review date falling due (**LIF-060**), a budget evaluation, an external source re-check (**LIB-035**), a translation job, indexing, a derivative rebuild, a scan timeout, a cohort run - must be visible to that tenant with its state, when it last ran, when it is next due and why it last failed. Work a user submits follows the job contract in **API-040** to **API-043**; this is the rest

A tenant must be able to see one declaration of everything that can leave its boundary: model endpoints (**GEN-031**), embedding (**GEN-038**), external reference sources (**LIB-037**), translation services (**LOC-026**), malware scanning (**AST-Q03**), data connections, webhooks and notification delivery. For each it must state what may leave, whether it is on by default, who may change it, and any residency constraint (**ADM-Q01**)

A tenant administrator must be able to grant, review and revoke support access (ADM-023) as an administrative act: each grant declaring its scope - metadata only, diagnostics, content read - its expiry, its purpose and who it is for, audited into the tenant's own log and shown in ADM-025. Support access must appear in the effective-permission view (**IAM-029**, **IAM-030**) like any other grant

Backup frequency, recovery point and recovery time must be declared per artifact class and tested: restoring must be exercised on a stated schedule rather than assumed, and a restore that is never rehearsed must not be presented as a capability (ADM-020)

Stored artifacts must have declared integrity re-verification schedules - assets against their hashes (**AST-042**), version digests (**VER-042**), audit exports (**LIF-055**) - and a verification failure must be surfaced in diagnostics and audited rather than logged

Every performance budget in the specification must be registered with its owner, its reference configuration, whether it is provisional, the tranche by which it is confirmed, and how it is measured in production. ADM-016's reporting must say, budget by budget, whether it is being met

Cost and usage attribution (ADM-010, ADM-011) must extend to every chargeable external operation: external reference searches, translation jobs, malware scanning, notification and email delivery, webhook delivery, indexing and embedding, and bulk generation
A tenant must be suspendable: sign-in and API access stop, content and configuration are retained untouched, the reason is recorded, and the suspension is reversible without loss

Before a tenant is closed, its administrator must be able to take a complete export of content, configuration and audit (**IMP-018**, ADM-039). Closure must not proceed until that export has been offered, and whether it was taken or declined must be recorded
Closing a tenant must be a deliberate, audited act with a declared grace period before anything is deleted, reversible throughout that period (**ADM-Q06**)
Suspension and closure must each declare in advance which capabilities stop and which continue - in-flight publications, scheduled work, webhook delivery - as ADM-014 does for an exhausted budget

Suspension and closure must each declare what stops and what continues, naming at least: shared publication links (**PUB-081**), webhook delivery, scheduled and background work (ADM-040), realtime connections, model endpoints, search indexes, notification delivery, and in-flight publications
Secrets must be held in a tenant-scoped store, write-only from any client's perspective (**DAT-003**)
A secret must be replaceable without being read, and rotation must not require a period where both values are invalid
Secrets must never appear in a log, a metric, a trace, an export, a crash report or an error, and each path must have a test
Access to a secret must be audited by the fact of access, never by its value
An administrator must be able to see what consumes a secret - which connections, model endpoints and scheduled work - before rotating it

Before rotating any tenant secret, an administrator must be able to see everything that consumes it: connections, model endpoints, external reference sources, translation services, scanning services, notification channels, webhook signing keys and scheduled work. A rotation that breaks something must be reported once against the secret, naming every dependent capability
AI token use must be attributable to a tenant, a user, a purpose and a document (**GEN-033**)
Query execution, storage, publication volume and asset storage must each be measured and attributable
A tenant administrator must be able to see cost trends, not only a current total
Budgets and alerts must be settable, and an alert must arrive before a limit rather than after
Where a budget is exhausted, what stops must be declared in advance: which capabilities degrade and which continue

Cost and usage must be presented as a trend over time, broken down per capability (ADM-010, ADM-011) and per period, with at least twelve months of history kept where the tenant has been running that long
A budget alert (ADM-013) must be delivered to named recipients through the notification channels **COL** owns (**COL-033**), and who receives it must be configurable by a tenant administrator

The precision at which usage is recorded, and how long usage records are kept, must be declared before measurement begins rather than inferred from the data afterwards (**LIF** owns retention policy; **ADM-Q02** can only raise the bar)
Health, latency and error rate must be measured per capability, not only for the service as a whole
The performance budgets in scope §11 must be measured in production as well as in tests, and the measurements must be reported against those budgets
A tenant administrator must be able to see diagnostics for their own tenant without raising a support ticket
Diagnostics visible to a tenant must contain no other tenant's data, and no content the viewer may not read
Failures that a user would experience as "nothing happened" - an index not updating, a webhook not delivering, a query timing out - must be surfaced rather than logged
Availability, recovery point and recovery time objectives must be stated, and actual availability, recovery point and recovery time must be measured against them
Degradation must be visible rather than silent: where a data source is unavailable, the product must say so (**scope §11**)

The diagnostics a tenant administrator can see (ADM-017) must include at least: health, latency and error rate per capability (ADM-015), the state of the search index, the delivery state of webhooks, the outcome of recent scheduled work, and the tenant's position against its budgets

Failures a user would experience as "nothing happened" - an index not updating, a webhook not delivering, a query timing out - must be surfaced to the tenant administrator in those diagnostics (ADM-036), and to the user waiting on the result where there is one
Support must be able to diagnose a tenant's problem without reading that tenant's content by default
Where access to content is genuinely needed, it must be granted by the tenant, time-bounded, scoped, and revocable
Every support access must be audited into the **tenant's own** audit log, visible to that tenant, not only into an internal one
A tenant must be able to see, at any time, whether support access is currently active and what it covers
Support tooling must make the difference between metadata and content obvious, so that reading content is a deliberate act
The product's own clients must use the same API as any other caller, with no privileged path
OpenAPI must be the source of truth for the synchronous surface, and client types must be generated from it
Contract tests must fail when the implementation and the specification disagree
Every capability the interface offers must be reachable through the API
Errors must be structured, with a stable machine-readable code alongside a human-readable message
An error must name what failed and, where relevant, which requirement or rule refused it
Listing endpoints must page consistently, with a stable order and an opaque cursor
Mutating requests must be idempotent when given an idempotency key, so that a retry cannot create a second document
Rate limits must be declared, and a limited response must say when to retry

A mutating request against a versioned resource must carry a precondition naming the version it was read at, and the server must refuse a mismatch with a distinct machine-readable code (API-005) naming the version the resource is at now
There must be no unconditional overwrite: a mutating request with no precondition must be refused rather than treated as latest-wins

A component lock (**COL-005**) must hold at the API exactly as it does in the interface: a mutating request against a component another identity holds must be refused, naming the holder and when the lock is expected to release (**COL-007**)
Every response must carry a request identifier, echoing the caller's own where one was given, and that identifier must appear in the server's logs and in any error the response reports (API-005)

The synchronous surface must declare availability and latency objectives of its own, and must be measured in production against them (**ADM-016**, **ADM-020**). Realtime already has one in API-036 (**API-Q07**)
Rate limits must be declared in the API specification itself, so that a contract test can verify them (API-003), and a limited response must say when to retry
Authentication and authorisation failures must follow the **IAM** contract and its distinction between unauthenticated and forbidden, rather than inventing a second vocabulary here

A realtime connection must re-check authorisation on a stated interval as well as at connect and reconnect (API-016), so that a permission withdrawn mid-connection takes effect without waiting for a reconnection that may never come (**IAM-067**)

Webhook subscriptions must be administrable: created, changed and removed by an entitled administrator, declaring the endpoint, the event types selected, and the signing key with a rotation path. Every such change must be audited (**LIF-064**), and subscriptions must be carried in the configuration export (**ADM-005**)

Every failure surfaced to a user, an administrator or an integrator must use the structured error contract in API-005 and API-006, with a stable machine-readable identifier. Every request, job, event, webhook delivery, realtime message, notification and publishing-pipeline stage must carry a correlation identifier that appears in logs, in diagnostics (**ADM-036**) and in any error reported about it

Submitting a job (API-040) or a bulk operation must be safely retryable: an idempotency key or equivalent must make a retry return the original work rather than starting a second export, publication, cohort or report. Where an operation cannot be idempotent, the specification must say what a retry does

Anything any area requires to be listable must be paged, capped or budgeted wherever its size grows with the tenant, with a stable order (API-007). A listing that cannot be paged must state its cap and show itself as capped (**SCH-034**)

Installing, updating and removing an extension must be permissioned, audited and visible to the tenant, and an extension must declare what leaves the tenant boundary so that it appears in the tenant's outbound inventory (**ADM-041**, API-033, **API-Q06**)
The API must be versioned, and a breaking change must require a new version rather than a note in a changelog
A deprecated version must be announced with a removal date, and must keep working until that date
Adding a field must never break a caller, and callers must be told to ignore fields they do not know
Deprecation must be visible in the response, not only in documentation
A new major API version must state what happens to the MCP surface: which tools move with it, which stay pinned to the older version, and when the older ones stop
Presence, locks, notifications and streaming model responses must be specified separately from OpenAPI, which cannot express them
That specification must be as authoritative as the OpenAPI one, and must be tested the same way
A realtime connection must authenticate and authorise exactly as a request does, and must re-check on reconnect
Realtime delivery must be at-least-once with client-side de-duplication, or must state plainly that it is not
A realtime client must converge on the current state from a snapshot on every connect and reconnect, so that no missed event can leave it wrong
A change to presence, a lock or the inbox must reach every connected viewer entitled to it within a stated interval - provisionally p95 of 250ms, never above one second
Work that can outlive a request must be submitted as a job and must return a job identity immediately, rather than holding the request open until it finishes
A job's state must be pollable - accepted, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled - with when it started and, where it is knowable, how far it has got
A job must be cancellable, and a cancelled job must state what it had already done and what it had not
A failed job must report its failure in the same structured shape as a synchronous error (API-005, API-006), and must remain inspectable after it has finished
Exporting at scale must be a job (**IMP-018**, **IMP-020**) rather than something a caller assembles by paging every resource
The MCP surface must be a small set of task-shaped tools over the API, never a generated mirror of it
Each tool must be described for a model rather than for a developer: what it is for, when to use it, and what it returns
A tool must act with the calling identity's permissions, with no path to exceeding them (**IAM-036**)
A tool that changes anything must be distinguishable from one that reads, and the distinction must be visible to the calling agent
Content returned to a model through MCP must be data, never instructions, on the same terms as **GEN-017**
Tool use must be audited with the identity, the tool, the arguments and the outcome
The number of tools must be kept small deliberately, and adding one must be a decision rather than a consequence of adding an endpoint
Content, workflow, review and publication events must be deliverable as webhooks
A webhook payload must say that something happened and identify it, and must not carry content the endpoint may not receive
Deliveries must be signed, so that a receiver can verify the sender
Failed deliveries must be retried with backoff, and a persistently failing endpoint must be disabled and reported
Deliveries must be inspectable by an administrator, including what was sent and what came back

Content, workflow, review, publication and notification events must be deliverable as webhooks. The inventory of events is owned by the areas that raise them - **COL-037**, **LIF**, **PUB** - and this area carries their delivery
Every delivery of one event must carry the same event identifier, so that a receiver which has already processed a delivery can discard a redelivery of it (API-028)

Webhook delivery must state plainly what ordering it guarantees. Where it guarantees none across event types, each event must carry what is needed to order it - the version or sequence it belongs to - so that a receiver can order what matters to it rather than trusting arrival order
Data source connectors must be addable without changing the product (**DAT-054**)
Output formats should be addable as extensions
Citation styles must be addable without a code change (**STY-023**)
An extension must declare what it needs and must run with no more authority than that
An extension failure must be attributable to the extension, never reported as a defect in the product
An extension must be updatable and removable, and removing one must state what depends on it before it is removed

Removing a connector must not alter or delete the content produced while it was installed. What becomes of bindings that depended on it must be stated - refused refresh, reported as unavailable (**DAT**) - and must never be silent staleness
An upload must be validated against a declared list of permitted formats, and anything not on it must be refused rather than stored
Format must be determined from the file's content, never from its name or the type a client claims
An upload must be scanned for malware before it can be referenced by anything
A size limit must be declared per format, and a tenant must be able to lower it

Ingest must record intrinsic properties: dimensions, resolution, colour space and page count where each applies, and duration only for a time-based format, which is admitted only if **AST-Q02** admits one
An asset whose intrinsic properties cannot be determined must be refused, because a style that cannot resolve is a failure deferred to publish
Ingest must strip or preserve embedded metadata according to a declared policy, and must record which it did
An upload awaiting its scan (AST-003) must be in a named quarantined state, visible to the uploader, and must not be referenceable, listable as available, or usable by anything until it clears
A scan that has not completed within a declared period must fail the upload rather than leaving it quarantined indefinitely, and the uploader must be told which happened either way
An upload that fails its scan must be refused, must never become referenceable, and the refusal must be audited without retaining the file anywhere content could reach it
The classes of file that may be an asset must be declared as a list, and a file outside it must be refused rather than stored as something content merely does not reference yet (AST-N03, **AST-Q05**)

Ingest must validate what a file expands to, not only the bytes it arrives as: decoded dimensions, decompressed size and nesting depth must each be bounded, and a file exceeding any of them must be refused
Ingest must record a content hash of the original, and that hash must be what identifies the bytes thereafter - for duplicate detection (AST-029), for export, and for verifying what is stored
A stored original must be verifiable against its hash on read, and re-verification on a schedule is the storage layer's (**ADM**). This area records the identity; storage keeps the promise
Thumbnails and preview renditions must be generated on ingest, not on demand
Browsing a library must use derivatives, so that a list of a thousand images is not a thousand originals
A derivative must be regenerable from the original, and must never be the only copy of anything
Format conversion for an output that cannot carry the original must be declared, and must be recorded on the publication
Converting a format for an output that cannot carry the original (AST-011) is a modification for licensing purposes, and must be refused where the licence does not permit modification (AST-022)

A conversion that changes the content as well as the container - a wide-gamut image reduced to sRGB, a transparency flattened - must be declared and recorded on the publication in the same way, because the picture a reader sees is not the picture that was ingested
A derivative must be discardable and rebuildable on demand from the original, which is what makes AST-010 worth having rather than a second permanent copy of everything
Replacing an original (AST-016) must rebuild or invalidate its derivatives, and a derivative of a superseded version must never be served for the version that replaced it
An asset must be able to carry default alternative text
A figure placing an asset must be able to override it, because the same photograph means different things in two documents (**CNT-017**)
Publishing must fail where neither the asset nor the figure supplies alternative text (**CNT-022**, **PUB-033**)
An asset that is purely decorative must be markable as such, so that it can be correctly given no alternative text

Default alternative text must carry the language it is written in, as a BCP 47 tag (**CNT-140**), so that it publishes as text in a known language (**CNT-084**). Where a figure overrides it (AST-013), the override takes the language of the component holding the figure
Replacing an asset must create a new version rather than overwriting it (**VER-011**)
A reference to an asset must be able to pin a version or float at latest, like any other reference
Where an asset is used must be listable, across components, documents and baselines (**REU-006**)
Deleting an asset must be refused while a baseline or publication depends on it (**VER-023**)
Deleting an asset used only by drafts must warn and name them

An asset version must state what it covers. The binary is versioned; the recorded properties - default alternative text, source, licence and permitted uses - must each carry their own history of what changed, when, and who changed it

A change to an asset's licence or to what it permits must be surfaced wherever the asset is used, as an expiry is (AST-025), and must never reach a reference floating at latest (AST-017) without being visible
Superseded asset versions must be retained and retrievable, together with the relationships between them: what replaced what, when, and why

A superseded version must not be separately deletable. Retention follows the asset and the retention policy over it (**LIF**), so that a version nothing currently references does not quietly become unavailable to an inspection that asks later
An asset must record its source and the licence it is held under
A licence must be able to declare what it permits: internal use, publication, redistribution, modification
Publishing must be refused where an asset's licence does not permit the use being made of it, and must say which asset and which licence
An asset carrying content credentials must have them preserved or deliberately removed, and which happened must be recorded
An expiry date must be recordable on a licence, and content past it must be surfaced wherever the asset is used

An asset with no recorded source or licence (AST-021) must be treated as internal use only: publishing it must be refused on the same terms as an asset whose licence forbids the use (AST-023), rather than proceeding because nothing was written down

Upload must ask for the source and licence declaration, and where it is not given must record its absence explicitly, so that undeclared assets are listable rather than indistinguishable from declared ones
A licence must be able to declare that it requires attribution, and what that attribution must say. Whether the credit line is rendered, and where, is **PUB**'s (**AST-Q06**)
Assets must belong to a space and must be permissioned by it (**IAM**)
Assets must be searchable by name, caption, alt text, format and metadata (**SCH**)
An asset library must be browsable visually, with filters
A duplicate upload should be detected by content, and the uploader offered the existing asset
Assets must be exportable with their metadata, and importable the same way (**IMP**)
Assets that nothing references - no component, no document, no baseline (AST-018) - must be listable, so that a library can be tidied deliberately rather than growing silently

The content schema must carry, in the first version ever stored, the node and mark types the neighbouring areas depend on - condition, suggestion and comment-anchor marks among them - even where the features that use them land in a later tranche
Content must be a tree of typed block nodes, serialised as JSON, structurally identical to what the editor manipulates in memory
Every block node must carry an identifier, allocated when the block is created, unique within its component, and never reused
Every annotation over a range of text must be a mark; marks must be able to cover overlapping ranges without nesting and without being split into separate annotations
Every mark must carry an identifier; an annotation fragmented across several text nodes must remain one annotation under one identifier
Accepting, rejecting or excluding a marked annotation must act on every fragment of that identifier in one operation
The mark vocabulary must be closed. Adding a mark type is a schema change with a migration, not a configuration option
The model must contain no mark or node whose only purpose is to represent an overlap, a range start or a range end
Marks must be semantic in intent. The model must carry no typeface, font size, colour or spacing
A resolution pass (accepting a suggestion, excluding a condition) must preserve block identifiers
Content must be validated on creation, on change, and on read-back from storage
Every stored content document must record the schema version it was written against
A migration path must exist from every schema version ever written to the current one, and must be exercised by a test carrying a fixture of each
Content that fails validation on read-back must be quarantined and reported, never silently coerced or partially loaded
A component must carry a title of its own, distinct from the title of any outline section that places it (**STR-005**), so that it can be listed and found in a space holding no documents at all
A component's title and base language (CNT-140) must be carried in its versioned content, so that a version records the title the component had when it was cut

A component's structural attributes - those every component carries whatever its type - must be a closed set: its identifier, its title, its base language, and the schema version its content was written against. Adding one is a schema change with a migration, not a configuration option
Paragraphs must be supported, as the default block

Lists must be supported - **ordered (numbered)**, unordered, and definition - nestable to at least six levels, with an author-settable start number and numbering format (decimal, alphabetic, roman) on an ordered list
Lists must be supported, in three kinds - **ordered (numbered)**, unordered and definition
A list must nest to at least six levels, in every kind and in any mixture of kinds
An ordered list must carry an author-settable start number and numbering format - decimal, alphabetic or roman - local to that list and independent of the outline's numbering (**STR**)
Authored tables must be supported, with header rows and columns, merged cells, and a caption
Figures must be supported, carrying a caption and alternative text, and referencing a managed asset rather than embedding one
Preformatted blocks must be supported, with an optional language label, preserving whitespace exactly
Block quotations must be supported, with an optional attribution that may carry a citation
Admonitions must be supported, from a closed vocabulary declared by the presentation theme
Admonitions must be supported, from the closed vocabulary the admonition style catalogue declares (**STY-003**)
Block-level equations must be supported
A figure's alternative text must be required, and publishing must fail when it is absent
Empty blocks used for vertical spacing must not be representable. Separation is a property of the presentation theme
A component must always hold at least one block. A newly created component must hold exactly one empty paragraph, as somewhere for the cursor to be

Every caption-bearing block - figure, table, block equation - must carry a stable identity, so the outline can number it and a cross-reference can target it (**STR** owns the sequences; **PUB** owns lists of figures and tables)

Every block must be addressable by its identifier, and any block must be able to be the target of a cross-reference (**STR** owns the reference itself). Carrying a caption is what makes a block numbered, not what makes it addressable
An image must be placeable inside a table cell

An image reference must carry a named **image style** chosen from a catalogue - `thumbnail`, `inline`, `column-width`, `full-width`, and whatever an administrator has added - and the publisher must resolve that style to real dimensions. The model must not carry pixel or point sizes
An image reference must carry a named **image style**, chosen from the image style catalogue (**STY**)
A named image style must be resolved to real dimensions at publish time, by the rules **STY** owns (STY-015 to STY-019), and the editor must resolve it by those same rules (STY-035)
An image reference must carry no pixel, point, millimetre or percentage dimension of its own
Resolving an image style must preserve the image's intrinsic aspect ratio. A style that fixes a width must derive the height from the image, and must never distort it
A style whose resolved height would exceed a declared maximum must be constrained by height instead, still preserving ratio. That maximum must be declared in the style, not discovered at publish time

Style catalogues must be configuration-extensible: an administrator must be able to add a style - "small thumbnail" - without a code change, and it must then be selectable by authors and honoured by every output format
A block must take its appearance from a named style chosen from a catalogue. Alignment, indentation and spacing must be properties of a style, never a free per-block toggle
Text must be the base inline node
Inline equations must be supported
Footnote anchors must be inline nodes (section 6)
Cross-references must be inline nodes carrying a target identity and what to display, never a resolved number or title
Citations must be inline nodes (section 8)
Variables must be supported, carrying a name resolved at publish time (**REU** owns resolution)
Inline data bindings must be supported, carrying a query reference (**DAT** owns resolution)
Character-level marks must be supported: **emphasis, strong, underline, subscript, superscript**, inline code, defined term and quoted phrase
Condition marks must be supported, carrying an axis and permitted values (**REU** owns evaluation)
Suggestion marks must be supported, carrying an operation and an author (**COL** owns the review workflow)
Comment anchor marks must be supported, carrying a thread identity (**COL** owns the thread)
The author must be able to apply and remove every mark in CNT-031 directly, from a toolbar and by keyboard shortcut. The editor must offer no control over typeface, font size or colour
Every component must declare a base language, and any run whose language differs from its surrounding context must carry its own language tag
A run's language must be carried through to every output format as the language of that passage

Every component must declare a base language, and any run whose language differs from its surrounding context must carry its own language tag. Every such tag must be a **BCP 47** language tag, carrying a region wherever the region changes the content - `pt-BR` distinct from `pt-PT`, `zh-Hans` from `zh-Hant`
An underline mark must be supported, and must be understood as the one mark named for its appearance rather than its meaning
An image must be placeable inline within a run of text
Hyperlinks must be supported, as a mark over a range of text carrying an absolute target and an optional title
A hyperlink's target must be validated against a declared allowlist of schemes - `http`, `https` and `mailto` at minimum - and a target with any other scheme must be refused on entry and never stored
A hyperlink must be carried to every output format: as a live link where the format has one, and otherwise as the rendering the theme declares (**STY**, **PUB**)
A footnote must be anchorable to a span of text
A footnote must be anchorable to a cell of an authored table
A footnote must be anchorable to a table as a whole
A footnote anchored into generated content must identify its target by data, never by position (**DAT** owns the binding case)
Footnote content must support paragraphs, the character marks in CNT-031, citations, inline equations and cross-references. It must **not** support tables or images
Footnote numbering must be a property of the outline, not of the component (**STR** owns it)
A footnote whose anchor cannot be resolved must fail the publish with a named error identifying the footnote

An authored table must be able to declare a key column, or set of columns. Where declared, a footnote must anchor to a cell by key value exactly as it does in a bound table. Where not declared, the anchor must fall back to row and column position, and must be marked as the weaker form because it does not survive a reorder

Footnote content must support paragraphs, the character marks in CNT-031, citations, inline equations, cross-references, hyperlinks, variables (CNT-029) and inline data bindings (CNT-030). The list is closed, and must **not** include tables or images
Equations must have one canonical stored representation, independent of how they were entered
An author must be able to enter an equation as LaTeX
An equation must render on screen, in PDF and in Word, from that one representation
An equation must be available in every context: running text, a heading, a table cell, a footnote and a caption
A block equation must be numbered or explicitly unnumbered; unnumbered equations must consume no number (**STR** owns the sequence)
An equation must carry an accessible textual alternative, generated where possible and author-editable
An equation that cannot be rendered in a target format must fail the publish, never render as source text or a blank
A citation must be a reference to a bibliography entry by identity. Typed citation text must not be representable
Bibliography entries must be managed artifacts within a space, referenceable from any component in it
A citation must be able to carry a locator - page, section, figure - alongside its reference
Citation and bibliography formatting must be applied at publish time from a selected style (**PUB** owns rendering)
A citation whose entry cannot be resolved must fail the publish, naming the citation and the component holding it
Citation styles must include at least CSE, Vancouver and Harvard, and the set must be extensible without a code change
The full Unicode range must be storable and renderable, including characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
Text must be normalised to a single Unicode normalisation form on ingest, so that two visually identical strings compare and search alike
An insertion palette must offer mathematical, Greek, and scientific and technical symbols
A tenant must be able to declare a list of preferred characters, surfaced first in that palette
Right-to-left and bidirectional text must be supported, with direction expressed in the model rather than left to styling
Paste from Word must preserve structure - headings, lists, tables, footnotes, emphasis - rather than producing styled runs
Paste from Markdown must preserve structure
Paste from HTML must preserve structure
Every paste must produce a report naming what was normalised and what was discarded, shown to the author at the time
Nothing discarded on paste may be absent from that report; the tests for paste must assert what was dropped as well as what survived
Pasted content must never carry typeface, size or colour into the model
Pasted HTML must be sanitised before it reaches the model: scripts, event handlers, embedded objects, and link targets whose scheme is not allowlisted (CNT-127) must never be stored
A hyperlink dropped or rewritten on paste must be named individually in the paste report (CNT-063), with the target it had

Content copied within the product must be re-identified when it is pasted: every block must receive a newly allocated identifier, unique within the receiving component and never one used before (CNT-002)

An annotation whose owning artifact does not travel with the content - a comment anchor, a suggestion - must be dropped when that content is pasted into another component, and named in the report (**COL** owns both)

Content written against an earlier schema version must be migrated to the current one before it enters the receiving component (CNT-012), or refused with a named error. It must never be stored unmigrated
Copying within the product must produce a report to the same standard as a foreign paste, naming what was re-identified and what was dropped (CNT-063, CNT-064)
Edits must be saved continuously and without an explicit save action, as iterations
An interrupted session - closed tab, lost connection, crash - must be recoverable to the last edit the author saw accepted
The editor must state plainly whether the current draft is saved, saving, or failing to save
Undo and redo must be scoped to the component being edited, must survive a reload within the session, and must reach back at least to the state the session opened from
A version must be cut on a **positive act** - an explicit save, or a deliberate release of the lock - and never on a keystroke, and never on the passage of time
Concurrent access is governed by soft component locks (**COL**); this area must not assume single-writer access

An iteration must not be a version: it must be immutable, timestamped, and visible only to the editor holding the lock. Iterations must be retained until the component's next version is cut, and for a declared window after that (**VER** owns the window)
An author must be able to see the iterations retained for the component they are editing, and restore any of them within that window
Undo must not cross a version boundary. Reaching further back than the version the session opened from is restoring an earlier version, which is a separate and audited act
The editor must check spelling as the author types
Spelling must be checked against the language of the run being edited (CNT-083), not against one language for the whole editor
A tenant must be able to maintain custom dictionaries, so that domain vocabulary is not flagged in every document
Spelling must behave identically in both deliveries. The browser supplies it; the desktop shell must wire the platform's checker through the platform bridge rather than silently losing it
A document must render as one continuous, visually consistent scroll, with its components inline
Component boundaries must be revealed on hover and by an explicit toggle, and must not be permanent chrome
The view must always show which component the cursor is in, whether this user may edit it right now, and **when they may not, why** - naming who holds the lock and when it is expected to release
Read-only rendering must be typographically identical to the editing view
The view must remain usable on a document assembling several hundred components (budget in scope §11)
The editing view must render the presentation theme's block spacing, so that the separation an author sees is the separation the output will have
The editing view must render the theme's typefaces at the sizes the theme declares, so that an author sees the type a reader will see
The editing view must set text at the measure of the document's publishing layout, scaled to the screen and zoomable, so that line lengths and relative image sizes are those of the output
An author must be able to preview the document as it will be published, in a selectable output format, without leaving the editor
Preview must be fast enough to use while writing rather than as a separate step, against the budget in CNT-136, tested
Preview must reflect an edit within one second, and never more than two, in a 300-page document - a provisional budget, to be confirmed against real content

Preview must reflect an edit within one second, and never more than two, in a 300-page document, measured on a declared reference configuration recorded alongside the budget - a provisional number, to be confirmed against real content (**CNT-Q13**)
The document view must operate in one of three modes - **read**, **review** or **author** - and must make the current mode obvious
The modes available to a user must be determined by their permissions (**IAM**), and a user must be able to drop to a less privileged mode deliberately
Each mode must offer only what it is for: read offers navigation and no editing affordances; review offers comments and suggestions but not direct edits; author offers direct editing
An author must be able to choose which version or revision of a component a document references, from the document view, without leaving it
Changing which version or revision a document references must be an audited act, recording who changed it, when, and from which to which
The view must show which version or revision of a component is referenced, and whether the reference is pinned or floating at latest

The view must show which version or revision of a component is referenced, and which of the three modes the reference takes: pinned, floating at latest, or tracking the latest approved revision (**REU-050**, **LIF-038**)
An author must be able to compare a component against an earlier version or revision from within the editor, choosing from a list that shows who changed each and when
That comparison must be available between any two versions and between any two revisions, rendered as a redline (**VER** owns the comparison itself)
An author must be able to see what they have changed in the current session, as a tracked-changes view over the version the session opened from
Every editing action must be reachable from the keyboard alone
The editor must meet WCAG 2.2 AA, verified rather than asserted
Structure - headings, lists, tables, footnotes - must be exposed to assistive technology as structure, not styling
Equations must be reachable and readable by assistive technology through their textual alternative
Inserting and resolving a suggestion or a comment must be announced to assistive technology, naming which annotation it was and what happened to it
Suggestions, comment anchors and redlines must be distinguishable without colour - by shape, border, marker or text - and must stay distinguishable in a high-contrast mode

CNT-078 must be verified by an automated accessibility suite run in continuous integration over the editor, and by a recorded manual audit against the WCAG 2.2 AA criteria before each release, the result kept as evidence. Conformance asserted without both is not conformance
A user must be able to see who else is in a document, and roughly where
Presence must show what each person is doing: reading, reviewing or editing (**CNT-104**)
Presence must respect permissions - a user must not be shown somebody working in a component they may not read
Presence must degrade to absence rather than to a wrong answer when a connection drops
A presence claim must be bounded by a declared heartbeat: a mode not refreshed within that period must be shown as stale, and then as absence, never as a live claim

Where a component is deleted or moved, locks and presence against it must degrade to absence exactly as a dropped connection does (COL-004), and threads anchored into it must be surfaced as orphaned (COL-017)
A component must be editable by one user at a time, and claiming it must be automatic on beginning to edit rather than a separate act
A lock must never prevent anybody from reading, commenting on or suggesting against the component
A held lock must be visible wherever the component appears, naming the holder and when it is expected to release (**CNT-074**)
A lock must release automatically after a declared period of inactivity, and the period must be a tenant setting
A lock must be takeable from an idle holder, with a warning, and the taking must be audited
Releasing a lock deliberately must cut a version; a lock timing out must not (**CNT-070**, **VER-003**)
Locks must be held per component, never per document, so that a report is worked on by several people at once

Where two users claim an unlocked component at once, exactly one must win. The loser must be told immediately, must never be shown an editable surface for a lock they do not hold, and must lose nothing they typed

When a lock is taken from its holder (COL-009), the holder's unsaved work must be kept as an iteration against that component (**CNT-089**), the holder must be told at once that the lock has gone and where their work is, and they must be able to recover it when they next hold the lock

Taking a lock (COL-009) must require the holder to have been idle for a declared period, which must be shorter than the automatic-release period (COL-008). Both must be tenant settings, and the taking period must never be set longer than the release period
A holder must be warned before their lock is taken and given a declared grace period in which any activity keeps it. Taking must never be instant, and must never be silent
A thread must be anchorable to a span of text, a component, a table cell, or an outline node
A thread must be resolvable, and resolving it must record who did so and when
A thread must support replies, and must show them in order with their authors
A mention must notify the person mentioned, and must respect whether they may read the thing discussed
A thread must survive the content around it changing
A thread whose anchor no longer exists must be surfaced as orphaned, never silently discarded
Threads must be listable for a whole document, filterable by state, author and age
Threads must not appear in published output in any form
A thread must be markable internal, and an internal thread must be invisible to external principals (**IAM-045**)
Whether a thread is internal must be evident to everybody who can see it, so that an internal thread is never mistaken for one the client has already read
A reply must inherit the internal marking of the thread it joins, and must never be able to widen it
A thread must not be deletable, by its author, by an author of the component, or by a tenant administrator. A thread that should not have been raised is resolved, and the record of it stays

Review metadata - threads, replies, suggestions, withdrawals, acceptances, rejections and round state - must be retained against the version it was made against, and must be removable through no product surface by anybody (**LIF-025**)
A comment may be edited by its author, and the earlier text must be retained in the record rather than replaced
A reviewer must be able to propose a change as a suggestion, rendered as a redline, without altering the content
A suggestion must be attributable to its author and its time
A suggestion must be acceptable or rejectable individually, and in bulk by author or by scope
Accepting or rejecting must act on the whole suggestion in one operation, across every fragment of it (**CNT-005**)
Accepting a suggestion must be audited, and must be attributable to the person who accepted it rather than to the person who proposed it
Suggestions must be visible against a locked component, so that review does not wait for an author to finish
An author must be able to see what they themselves changed in the current session, distinctly from what others have suggested (**CNT-113**)
Unresolved suggestions must be reportable, and a lifecycle gate must be able to require that there are none (**LIF**)
Accepting or rejecting a suggestion writes to the component and is therefore an edit: the person doing it must hold the lock, claimed automatically where the component is free (COL-005)
Where another user holds the lock, accepting or rejecting must be refused, naming the holder and when the lock is expected to release (COL-007). The suggestion must stay pending

A suggestion must only ever be applied by a deliberate act of a person holding the lock. Nothing must apply one automatically - not a lock releasing, not a timeout, not a round closing, and not a queue of decisions taken earlier

The author of a suggestion must be able to withdraw it while it is unresolved. A withdrawal must record who and when, exactly as a rejection does, and must not remove the record that the suggestion was made

Where accepting one suggestion leaves another no longer applicable, the second must be surfaced as stale, saying what happened to it. It must never be silently dropped, and must never be rejected on its author's behalf
A review round must name its reviewers, its scope and its due date
Each reviewer's state must be visible: not started, in progress, or complete
"Has everybody reviewed this" must be answerable without asking anybody
A round must be able to be run against a baseline, so that reviewers see a fixed document rather than a moving one
A reviewer must be able to record that they have finished with nothing to say, which is different from not having looked
A reviewer's completion must be reversible while the round is open, and reopening must be recorded with who and when
"Has everybody reviewed this" (COL-030) must be answered from explicit completion alone (COL-029, COL-032). Inactivity must never be read as completion
A review round must be able to name an external principal as a reviewer on the same terms as an internal one; what that principal may then do remains **IAM**'s (**IAM-045**)
Notifications must be deliverable in an in-app inbox and by email
A user must be able to choose what they are notified about and how often
Notifications must be digestible into a single message rather than one per event
A notification must not disclose content the recipient may not read - it must say that something happened, not what
Notification events must also be available as webhooks (**API**)

Notification channels must be tenant configuration: which channels are enabled, the address or domain email is sent from, and the tenant's own policy. Changing that must be permissioned and audited, and must be carried in the configuration export (**ADM-005**, **ADM-027**)

Notification delivery must state its guarantee: at-least-once with a stable event identifier a recipient can de-duplicate on (**API-045**), a declared retry and backoff, and a failing channel surfaced in tenant diagnostics (**ADM-036**) rather than silently dropped

The inbox must have a stated lifecycle: how long a notification is retained, who may delete one, what happens to a deprovisioned user's inbox, and that its contents are a second copy of tenant content and tenant-scoped as such (**IAM-066**)

The rule in COL-036 must hold wherever review material leaves the document: a report of unresolved suggestions (COL-027), an export, a digest and a webhook payload (COL-037) must each carry no content the recipient may not read

Every time this area records - a suggestion's time, a resolution, an expected lock release, a round's due date - must be stored as an absolute instant, displayed in the reader's own time zone, and shown as an instant rather than as a bare calendar day
A connection must be a tenant-owned, named, configured route to one source system
Connection types must include at minimum a relational database, an HTTP endpoint, and a file-based source such as a spreadsheet or delimited file
A connection's credentials must be held in a tenant secret store and must be write-only from a client's perspective
Reading a connection's settings must return whether a credential is set, and never the credential
A credential must not be capable of appearing in a log, a telemetry event, an export, a crash report or an error message, and a test must assert each path
A connection must be testable from the interface, and the test must report success or a reason without echoing the credential
Creating, changing and deleting a connection must be audited, including which fields changed but never their values
A connection must declare how queries against it authenticate: as a tenant service account, or as the end user
A connection must record where it is used - which query definitions, and through them which documents - and deleting one must show that before it proceeds, as DAT-016 does for a query definition
Deleting a connection that a query definition still references must be refused, naming what depends on it. It must never cascade, and must never leave a query pointing at nothing

Rotating a connection's credentials must not change what any query resolves to. Where a rotation leaves queries unable to authenticate, the connection must be reported as failing once, naming every dependent query, rather than surfacing one broken document at a time (**ADM-047**)
A query definition must be a named, versioned artifact belonging to a space, and must reference exactly one connection
A query definition must declare its parameters: name, type, whether required, and the permitted values or range of each
A query definition must declare the shape of its result: the columns it returns and their types
A query definition feeding a table that anything may be anchored to must declare a key column, or set of columns, that identifies a row
Query definitions must be reviewable and permissioned like content, and changing one must be audited
A query definition must be runnable against sample parameters from the interface, showing the result, before any document depends on it
Changing a query definition must create a new version, and a binding must be able to pin a version or float at latest
A query definition must record where it is used, so that changing one shows what it will affect before the change is made
A query definition must declare whether an empty result is valid for it, so that returning no rows can be told apart from failing to run
A parameter must be passed to the source as a bound value, and must never be concatenated into query text
A parameter must not be able to change the shape of a query. Table names, column lists, predicates and fragments of query language must not be parameterisable
Where a query genuinely needs to vary - a sort column, a chosen unit - the variation must be chosen from a list the query definition declares, never supplied as free text
Every parameter value must be validated against its declaration before the query runs, and a value that fails must produce a named error rather than an empty result
Injection must be attempted through every parameter type by a test, and refused
Which identity a query runs as must follow the connection's declaration (DAT-008), and must be visible to any author using that query
Under end-user pass-through, the source system's own access rules must apply, and results may legitimately differ between two users of the same document
Where results can differ by user, a pinned value must record whose view produced it, and the document must be able to show that
Permission to use a connection at all must be granted separately from permission to read a document that uses it (**IAM-020**)
A cached result obtained under one user's identity must never be served to another (**§11**)
An inline binding must substitute a single value into running text
A block binding must produce a table, and its presentation must be **TAB**'s and **STY**'s rather than the binding's
A binding must name a query definition, the parameters to run it with, and - for an inline binding - which value of the result to take
A binding must be able to take a parameter from the document's parameter set as well as from a literal, so that one component serves many documents
An inline binding whose query returns more than one value must fail with a named error, and must never silently take the first
An inline binding whose query returns no value must fail, and must never render as an empty string
How a bound value is formatted must come from a style, not be stored in the binding (**STY**, **TAB**)

An inline binding must identify the value it takes in one of two ways: from a result of exactly one row, naming the column; or by naming the key value of a row (DAT-012) and the column. A binding that identifies neither must be refused when it is written, not when it runs
An author must be able to revise a resolved value in place - an inline bound value, or a cell of a bound table - without editing the query definition or the binding

A revision must never replace what the query returned. The binding must retain the resolved value, the value a person entered, who entered it, when, and the reason they gave, and the revision must be audited with what it was and what it became
A revised value must be marked as revised by a person wherever it appears - in the editor, in review and in published output - and must never be indistinguishable from a value a query produced

A revised binding must stay refreshable. Where the source value moves (DAT-036), the binding must be flagged, the source value must be shown beside the revision, and the author must accept or reject the change deliberately. A refresh must never silently discard a revision, and must never silently keep one over a source that has changed
An outstanding revision must be surfaced to reviewers as something to review, and a lifecycle gate must be able to require that a document has none before it is issued (**COL**, **LIF**)

Provenance (DAT-040) for a revised value must record both halves: what the query returned, and the revision that stands in front of it. "Where did this number come from" must be answerable as "a person changed it, and here is what the query said"

A revision to a cell of a bound table must be anchored by key (DAT-012), and a revision whose row the query no longer returns must produce a named diagnostic identifying the revision, the key and the query, exactly as DAT-048 does for a footnote
Every binding must resolve in one of three modes: live, pinned, or refreshable
A pinned binding must store the value it resolved to, together with its provenance
A refreshable binding must be flagged when its source has moved since it was pinned
Refreshing a binding must be an explicit act, and must be audited with what it was and what it became
A baseline must pin every binding it contains regardless of mode, so that a published document always resolves to what it published
An author must be able to see, for a whole document, which bindings are stale, which have failed, and which have never resolved

A binding floating at latest (DAT-015) must be flagged when the query definition it floats on advances, in the same way DAT-036 flags a source that has moved, and a document must be able to show which of its bindings have changed meaning since it was last published

Refreshing, pinning or revising a binding is a change to the component holding it, and must be governed by the same concurrency rules as any other edit: the component lock (**COL-005**, **COL-041**) and the API's version precondition (**API-037**). Last-write-wins must not be the answer

Every resolved binding must write a provenance record: the query definition and its version, the parameters, the connection, the execution identity, the time, the row count, and a checksum of the result
Provenance must be inspectable from the value as it appears in the document, in one step
A publication must be accompanied by the provenance of every bound value in it
A provenance record must be immutable, and must be retained for as long as the baseline that references it
A query that fails must fail the publish with a named error identifying the query, the binding and the document
A result that was truncated must be treated as a failure, and must never be published as though it were complete
A binding must never publish a blank, a zero, or a placeholder in place of a value it could not resolve
In the editor, a failed binding must show in place with its reason, and the rest of the draft must still render
A footnote anchored to a row the query no longer returns must produce a named diagnostic identifying the footnote, the key and the query
Every diagnostic must be attributable to a connector, a query, or the product, so that a failing source is not reported as a defect in the document

Where a query definition declares an empty result invalid (DAT-068), returning no rows must fail exactly as a failure does (DAT-044). Where it declares one valid, the table must publish with its headers and a declared statement that there is nothing to show, never as blank space a reader cannot tell from a defect (**TAB** owns the rendering)
A query definition must declare a row limit, a result size limit and a timeout, and a tenant must be able to lower them
Exceeding any limit must be a named failure rather than a truncated result
A query definition must be able to declare how long its result may be cached, and the default must be no caching rather than some
Query execution volume and cost must be attributable to a tenant, a query and a document (**ADM**)

The total volume of query execution a tenant may run at once - across documents, baselines, refreshes and publications - must be limited and throttled, and this area owns that limit (**ADM** owns reporting its cost, DAT-053). A throttled execution must be a named, retryable failure, never a truncated or partial result (DAT-045, DAT-051) (**DAT-Q06**)
New source types must be addable as connectors without changing the product (scope §7.15)
A connector must declare its capabilities - parameter binding, key columns, row limits, pass-through identity - and the product must refuse to rely on one it has not declared
A connector must run with no more authority than the connection it serves

Where a connector can report cheaply that data has changed - a row version, an entity tag, a modified timestamp - it must declare that as a capability (DAT-055), and staleness detection (DAT-036) must use what is declared rather than re-running the query to find out
A prompt must be a named, versioned artifact in a prompt library, reviewable like a query definition
A prompt must declare its context explicitly: which metadata, which components, which query results it may see
Context must never be implicit. A prompt must not receive anything it did not declare
A prompt must declare what it may produce: which component or field, and of what kind
A prompt must declare which model or class of model it expects, and must fail rather than silently running against another
Running a prompt must record the prompt version, the model and its version, the parameters, and a digest of the context it was given

The context digest in GEN-006 and GEN-023 must be one value, computed once from the context as it was actually given to the model, in a canonical order, and recorded identically on the run and on the content. Two digests that could differ would break provenance matching without failing anything

Where a declared context exceeds what the chosen model can accept, the run must be refused or the overflow surfaced for a person to resolve. Context must never be silently truncated, which is GEN-003's implicit context arriving from the other direction

Reviewing and approving a prompt version must use the same workflow machinery as any other reviewed artifact (**LIF-007** to **LIF-013**), and what approval means for a prompt - who may give it, and against what evidence (**GEN-Q03**) - must be stated rather than inherited by analogy with a query definition

A run record, a context digest and an acceptance must be retained for at least as long as the content version they describe (**LIF** owns the policy), because GEN-026 is only answerable while they exist

A prompt must be able to declare its context as a combination of components rather than only as a fixed list: by position in the structure outline (**STR**), by relationship (**REL**), by metadata match, and by the document's own parameter set (**TPL**)

A context declared that way must resolve to an enumerable set before the model is called, and what it resolved to must be recorded on the run (GEN-006) and inspectable afterwards (GEN-016). "Which components did this see" must be answerable for every run

Resolving a context specification must apply the requesting user's permissions (GEN-013, GEN-014) and must never widen what that user could read themselves. A specification is a way of naming components, never a way of reaching them
Where a specification resolves to nothing, or to more than the model can accept (GEN-043), the run must fail or surface it rather than proceeding against a subset nobody chose
The assistant's tools must be the product's own capabilities - search, read, propose an edit, run a declared query - and nothing else
Every tool call must be authorised exactly as the equivalent user action would be, using the calling user's identity (**IAM-036**)
A tool call that changes anything must be confirmed by the user before it takes effect
The assistant must show what it did: which tools it called, with what arguments, and what came back
The assistant must be able to cite the content it drew on, by identity, so that a claim can be checked
A thin assistant capability must be available from T2 - drafting against the current document - so that this governance is exercised early
A user must be able to hold an interactive conversation with a model, putting their own prompts to it rather than only running a declared one from a library

An open prompt must run under exactly the governance a declared one does: the calling identity's permissions (GEN-008), retrieval filtered before anything reaches the model (GEN-013, GEN-014), content as data (GEN-017), output as a marked proposal (GEN-022, GEN-024), and the run recorded (GEN-006)

Guardrails must be declared and enforced on both what is sent and what comes back, and a tenant must be able to state what it forbids. A refusal must say that it refused and why, never fail silently (GEN-021)

A question unrelated to the product must not be refused for being unrelated. What is refused is what the guardrails forbid; the boundary that protects a tenant is what the assistant may do (GEN-007), not what it may be asked

A user must be able to choose, within a conversation, from the model endpoints the tenant administrator has configured (GEN-027, GEN-028). The endpoint in use must be visible, including whether it sits outside the tenant's data boundary (GEN-031)

Tool use within a conversation must be able to create and update components, with every change confirmed before it takes effect (GEN-009), arriving as a proposal (GEN-024), and marked as generated until accepted (GEN-022)

Accepting or applying generated content - an assistant's proposed edit, an inserted citation, a tool call that writes - is a write to the target artifact and must obey exactly the rules any other edit obeys: the component lock (**COL-005**, **COL-041**), refusal naming the holder where another identity holds it (**COL-042**), and the version precondition at the API (**API-037**). Nothing may be applied automatically while somebody else holds the lock

Retrieval within a conversation must be interactive: a user must be able to see what was retrieved, add to it, remove from it and re-run, and every change must be re-filtered by their permissions rather than trusted because it was already shown

A user must be able to save their own prompts to a personal prompt library, visible only to them, and to run one in a conversation. A personal prompt is not a tenant artifact: it must never be bound by a template (**TPL-002**) or run by anybody else

Promoting a personal prompt into the tenant's library must be a deliberate act, after which it is a named, versioned, reviewed artifact like any other (GEN-001, GEN-045). There must be no path by which a personal prompt becomes a shared one without that act
Retrieval must be over the tenant's own content, and must be filtered by the requesting user's permissions before anything reaches a model
A model must never be given content the requesting user could not read themselves
Retrieval must not cross a tenant boundary under any circumstance (**IAM-001**)
What was retrieved must be inspectable by the user, so that a wrong answer can be traced to what it was given
Component content, imported documents, query results and comments must be treated as data, never as instructions
Text within retrieved content that addresses the assistant must not change what it does, and must not be acted on
No content may raise the authority of a tool call. Authorisation must come from the calling identity and from nowhere else (**GEN-008**)
Injection must be attempted by tests through every path content reaches a model - a component, an imported document, a query result, a comment - and must fail
Where the assistant declines to follow an instruction found in content, it should say so, because a silent refusal looks like a failure to understand
Generated content must be marked as generated, and must remain marked until a human accepts it
Generated content must record the model, its version, the prompt version and a digest of its context
Generated content must be a proposal until accepted, and acceptance must be an audited act naming the person who accepted
Publishing must be refusable where unaccepted generated content remains, and a lifecycle gate must be able to require none
It must be possible to report, for any document, which of its content originated from a model and who accepted it
A generated proposal must have a terminal state when it is not accepted: discarding it must be an explicit act, recorded with who discarded it and when
Discarding must not purge the record. What was proposed, by which prompt and model, and that a person discarded it, must remain reportable (GEN-026)
Only a proposal still outstanding may block publishing (GEN-025). A discarded proposal must not, and a document must never be left unpublishable by a draft somebody threw away
A tenant must be able to configure multiple model endpoints, across providers, including self-hosted ones
A tenant must be able to route by purpose, so that drafting and summarising need not use the same model
Endpoint credentials must be held as secrets, on the same terms as data connections (**DAT-003**)
A tenant must be able to bring its own provider account
Where a model endpoint is outside the tenant's data boundary, that must be stated in configuration rather than discovered

Computing an embedding is a model call and is subject to GEN-027 and GEN-031 on the same terms as generation, so a tenant that will not send content beyond its boundary must be able to embed within it or to have no semantic search at all (**SCH-013**)
A model that is unavailable must fail visibly; the product must not silently fall back to a different one
Token use must be attributable to a tenant, a user, a purpose and a document
A tenant must be able to set budgets and receive alerts before they are reached
Per-user rate limits must be settable
Prompt and result caching must be available, and must never serve one user's result to another (**DAT-026**)
Cost must be visible to the user incurring it, not only to an administrator

Embedding must be attributable and budgeted on the same terms as generation (GEN-033, GEN-034). Re-embedding a corpus must be costed and shown before it runs, because it is the one model call that happens once per component rather than once per question
Every artifact must belong to exactly one tenant, and no artifact may be shared between tenants

Tenant isolation must be enforced at the data layer, not by application code remembering to add a filter: a schema per tenant, and a database role assumed for the duration of one transaction ([ADR-0008](../../decisions/0008-schema-per-tenant-isolation.md), [ADR-0020](../../decisions/0020-service-foundations-tenant-roles-zod-first-apis-kysely.md))
The tenant a request acts within must be derived from the authenticated session, and never from a parameter the caller supplies
Every read and write path must be covered by a test that attempts access from a second tenant and is refused
Search indexes, caches, secrets, model endpoints, publications and the audit log must each be tenant-scoped, not only the content

IAM-005's list must be read as examples of one rule: every second copy, derived representation or outbound payload of tenant content must be tenant-scoped and permissioned like the content it derives from. That includes search indexes, caches, embeddings and vectors, asset derivatives, export artifacts, notification messages and digests, webhook payloads, audit exports and backups, and every path must be covered by a test like IAM-004's
Deleting a tenant must render everything it owns unreadable on a stated timetable, and that timetable must be verifiable

A customer must be able to hold several tenants - production, a sandbox, a validation environment - grouped by an organisation that shares billing, administration and identity provider configuration, and never content
Each tenant must be reachable at its own hostname, two-level names such as an environment under a customer's name included, and a customer's own domain must be addable without a code change

The timetable in IAM-006 must be a stated number of days from the deletion becoming irreversible to everything the tenant owns being unreadable, published to tenants in advance, and proven by a test rather than asserted. It is the same clock as the grace period in **ADM-030** (**IAM-Q08**)
A tenant must be able to federate authentication with its own identity provider over OIDC
Users should be provisioned and de-provisioned by SCIM where the customer supports it, with a documented manual path where they do not
Group membership asserted by the identity provider must be mappable to roles, so that access follows the customer's own directory
A user disabled at the identity provider must lose access without waiting for a token to expire
A tenant must be able to federate with more than one identity provider, because contractors and acquisitions do not share a directory
Authentication must be re-assertable within a session, so that a signing act can require it (**LIF** owns when)
Every authentication, and every authorisation that resulted in a refusal, must be recorded in the audit log (**LIF** owns the log)
A tenant with no identity provider configured must be able to authenticate its users by Google account, so that an evaluation or a small deployment works before any federation exists
The product must never store, reset or transmit a password. There must be no local credential of any kind, for any user, including an administrator
A tenant must declare which authentication routes it permits - its own provider, Google accounts, or both - and must be able to close a route once it no longer needs it

A tenant accepting Google accounts must say who may enter by that route - the addresses it has invited, and any Google Workspace domains it names - because any Google account can authenticate, and authenticating must never be enough to enter
Only basic identity scopes may be requested from an account provider - `openid`, `email` and `profile` - and a scope that is sensitive or restricted must never be requested

A session or a token must be checkable against current state on every request, so that a disablement (IAM-010) or a revocation (IAM-035) takes effect at the next request rather than at the next expiry. A long-lived bearer token whose validity cannot be established without asking its issuer must not be the only credential a caller holds (**IAM-Q07**)

A change to a user's group membership at the identity provider must take effect within a stated bound: applied on receipt where the provider pushes it (IAM-008), and otherwise re-read at a declared interval and at every re-authentication. The bound must be stated and tested, not left to whenever a token happens to be renewed

Where a tenant's identity provider is unreachable, or its signing keys cannot be fetched or verified, authentication must fail closed. A cached assertion must never outlive the session it authenticated, and no route may open because another is unavailable (**IAM-Q09**)
Signing-key rotation at a provider must be picked up without a manual step, and a key that cannot be resolved must refuse the authentication rather than accept an assertion it cannot verify

Signing out (IAM-039) or revoking a token (IAM-035) must stop further authorised data flowing on any connection already open, within a stated bound, and must not wait for that connection to end. A connection that cannot be terminated must stop delivering and must surface an authentication failure rather than continuing quietly

An organisation (IAM-052) must have administrators of its own, and organisation-level acts - creating a tenant, suspending one, changing the identity-provider configuration the organisation shares - must be permissioned through roles and audited into both the organisation's record and the affected tenant's own log

An organisation administrator must see only administrative metadata about its tenants - existence, state, configuration, usage and cost - and never their content. The tenant boundary (IAM-001) is not weakened by the grouping above it

The permission model must name high-risk administrative acts separately from `administer`, each grantable through a role and explainable in the effective-permission view (IAM-029 to IAM-031): whole-tenant export, audit-log export, applying and releasing a legal hold, initiating suspension or closure, granting support access, rotating a secret, configuring an external service, and configuring webhooks or notification channels

The first administrator of a new tenant must arrive by an invitation to a named address, authenticated by a route IAM-043 permits, and must never be created by a local credential (IAM-042) or by a vendor account that outlives the bootstrap (**ADM-Q04**)
Bootstrapping a tenant must be audited into that tenant's own log: who invited the first administrator, when, under what authority, and when the vendor's part in it ended

No standing vendor access may remain after bootstrap. Any later vendor action inside a tenant must go through the support-access path that the tenant grants, bounds and can revoke (**ADM-022** to **ADM-025**)
A space must belong to exactly one tenant, and must be the primary unit of access control below it
Content must be movable between spaces within a tenant, and moving it must re-evaluate its permissions rather than carrying the old ones
A component in one space must be referenceable from a document in another only where the referring user may read it
That permission must be re-checked when the document is published, not only when the reference was created, because access changes and publication is what escapes
Permissions must be declarable at tenant, space, template, document and component level
The permission set must cover at least: read, create, edit, comment, suggest, approve, publish and administer
The right to see a data connection's results must be separately grantable from the right to read the document containing them
