Versions must be numbered sequentially within their revision, and the pair must be presentable as `revision.version`
Every version must record the schema version its content was written against (**CNT-011**)
Documents, outlines, assets, query definitions, themes, layouts and templates must each be versioned by the same rules as content

Immutability must mean more than an absence of writes: every version must record a content digest over its canonical serialisation, and that digest must be recomputable from the content by anybody holding it, so that tampering is detectable rather than only forbidden
Every recorded time must be an absolute instant in UTC (**LIF-062**), and the order of a chain must come from its sequence rather than from the clock, so that skew cannot reorder history
A revision must be a designation applied to an existing version, not a second snapshot beside it
A revision must be created only when a lifecycle gate is passed (**LIF**), never by an author acting alone
A revision must record who designated it, when, and against which gate
Revisions must be numbered sequentially from 1, and something never issued must be presentable as revision 0
A revision must be immutable once designated, including its number
A baseline must be a named, immutable version of a whole document

A baseline must pin the exact version of every component, asset, query definition, theme, typeface, layout and citation style the document used, and the outline itself (**STY-047** is what makes a typeface pinnable)
A baseline must pin every bound value and its provenance, regardless of the binding's mode (**DAT-038**)
A baseline must record the conditions in force when it was taken, because a document has as many resolutions as it has profiles
Creating a baseline must be an explicit act, and must be possible automatically at a lifecycle gate
A baseline must be reproducible: everything it pins must remain retrievable for as long as the baseline exists
Deleting anything a baseline pins must be refused while that baseline exists

A baseline must also pin what VER-018 does not name and resolved output still depends on: the bibliography entries, terms and vocabulary values the document references (**LIB-004**), and the template version recorded on it with the definitions that version owned (**TPL-025**, **TPL-043**)
A baseline must record a digest over the set of versions it pins, so that "these are the exact inputs" is one value somebody can check rather than a list they must compare by hand (VER-042)
A baseline's name must be unique within its document and must not be changeable after creation, because the name is part of what an immutable record is cited by

A baseline must be markable as superseded, recording what superseded it, and a superseded baseline must remain retrievable. Baselines accumulate by design - nothing deletes one (VER-023) - so the controls are that creating one is a positive act and that a list can be filtered by state
Who may read a version history, run a comparison or export a redline must follow the permissions of what is being compared (**IAM**), and an export must carry no content its requester may not read

Comparison must meet a stated budget for a document of several hundred components with a history of hundreds of versions - provisional, confirmed against real content, measured in production like every other budget (**ADM-016**)

Comparison must be available at three levels: **structural**, what moved, was added or removed in the outline; **content**, what changed inside a component; and **resolved output**, what changed in the published result
Comparison must be possible between any two versions of a component, and between any two baselines of a document
Comparison must be possible across a template version change
A block that moved and was reworded must report as one change, not as a deletion and an insertion
Matching must use block identity where it exists, and content similarity where it does not
Every reported change must state how it was matched - by identity or by similarity - because a reader needs to know how far to trust it
A comparison must render as a redline, and must be exportable
Resolved-output comparison must catch changes caused by data, conditions or definition versions rather than by anyone editing

Comparison must be possible between two baselines of a document created under different template versions, and must separate what differs because a definition changed from what differs because somebody edited (VER-031's distinction, applied to a template's definitions)
Restoring an earlier version must create a new version whose content matches it. Nothing must ever be rewritten
A restore must record what it restored from, so the history reads as a decision rather than a mystery
Restoring must be refused where it would leave a baseline unable to resolve
An author must be able to preview what a restore would produce before it happens

Restoring must be refused where the restored content would reference something that no longer resolves - a component version since deleted, an asset removed - and the refusal must name what is missing. A restore adds a version rather than rewriting one, so it can never leave an existing baseline unable to resolve (VER-022, VER-032)
Versions, revisions and baselines must be retained for as long as the tenant keeps its content, subject to policy (**LIF**)
Retention and legal hold must be able to prevent deletion of anything a baseline depends on
Erasure of personal data must be reconcilable with immutable history by design, not by exception - what is erased and what remains must be stated

Deleting a component or a document must state what happens to its version chain: the chain must be retained under retention policy (**LIF-024**) and remain readable to audit, or the deletion must be refused. A chain must never be left orphaned - unreachable and undeleted

Where a chain is retained after the artifact it belonged to is deleted, what remains must be stated: its identity, its versions and the audit of them, with content removed only where erasure required it (VER-038, **LIF-024**)
Data derived from a version - an embedding above all - must record the model and the model version that produced it
Re-deriving must insert new derived data and must alter no version, so that changing model is an operation rather than a rewrite of history
A baseline must remain re-publishable on the engine version recorded with its publication (**PUB-063**) for as long as the baseline exists

The engine versions a baseline may need must be retained and runnable for as long as that baseline exists, and the cost of keeping them must be visible to whoever sets retention (**PUB-063**, **ADM**)

nonRequirements.statement: **No standing support access to tenant content** (ADM-023)

**No cross-tenant reporting** of content, or of product analytics identifying individuals or unrelated tenants, other than aggregates that identify nobody. Administrative and cost reporting across the tenants of one customer organisation is permitted to that organisation's own administrators (**IAM-068**, **IAM-069**), because they are one customer looking at themselves
**Not a billing system.** Usage is measured and reported here; invoicing is somewhere else
**No configuration only reachable by the vendor.** Anything a tenant is entitled to change, a tenant administrator can change
**Not a notification system.** This area decides what is worth alerting on and who should receive it; the inbox, the email and the delivery are **COL**'s (COL-033 to COL-036)
**No MCP surface generated from the API** (API-018)
**No privileged internal API** that the product's own clients use and others cannot (API-001)
**No arbitrary code execution as an extension point.** Extensions are declared and sandboxed, or they are not extensions
**No GraphQL surface alongside the REST one**, unless something forces it. Two APIs are two contracts and two sets of bugs

**No unattended bulk import through the API.** Bringing foreign content in is **IMP**'s attended flow (IMP-001 to IMP-003): a proposal a person accepts, and a report of what was dropped. An endpoint that skipped it would skip the person
**Not a digital asset management product.** This manages the assets used in documents, not a media library for a business
**No image editing.** Cropping, retouching and annotating happen elsewhere; an asset arrives finished
**No arbitrary file storage.** An asset is something content references, not an attachment locker
**No embedding of an original where a derivative will do**, and no derivative that cannot be regenerated

**No typeface, font size or colour _chosen by the author_.** The editor renders the theme's typefaces at the theme's sizes (CNT-097) - what the author cannot do is pick a different one. Narrower than "no styling" on purpose - see CNT-035
**No page geometry in content.** Page size, margins, running heads and columns belong to the publishing layout. Whether a forced page break is an exception is **CNT-Q07**
**No free-form drawing or diagramming.** A figure references a managed asset produced elsewhere
**No embedded spreadsheets or live formulas.** Computation belongs in the query layer
**No arbitrary HTML or raw markup escape hatch.** It would defeat every guarantee in section 3
**No per-author formatting preferences.** Two authors editing one document must produce content that looks the same
**No tables or images inside footnotes** (CNT-129, which superseded CNT-040)

**No per-document override of a theme's styles.** Where a document needs a different look it uses a different theme, which an administrator configures. Otherwise every document drifts into being its own theme

**No headings in component content.** A component carries no heading, because the outline owns structure and its titles (**STR**) - and because a component that knew its own heading level could not be used at two depths. A decision, not an omission

**No link to content inside the product expressed as a URL.** An internal target is a cross-reference (CNT-027), which survives a move, a rename and a renumber. A URL to a component would be a second, weaker way of doing the same thing
**No real-time character-level co-editing.** Scope §9 decision 4; the parallelism authors want is across components (**COL-011**)
**No document-level locking.** It defeats the point of components
**No comments in published output** (COL-019)
**No anonymous review.** Every comment, suggestion and acceptance is attributable, because an audited document cannot contain unattributed changes
**No live cursors.** Presence says which component each person is in and their mode (COL-001, COL-002), not where their cursor is; cursor-level presence belongs to the co-editing COL-N01 rules out
**No deleting review history.** Not by its author, not by an author of the component, not by a tenant administrator (COL-049, COL-050). Resolution is how a thread stops mattering
**No queued or automatic application of a suggestion** (COL-043). A change to a document is made by a person, at a moment they chose, against the content in front of them
**Not an ETL tool.** Reshaping, joining and aggregating happen in the source or in the query, not in a pipeline this product owns
**No writing back to a source.** Every connection is read-only, and a connector that could write would make this product part of somebody's change-control boundary
**No ad-hoc queries written by document authors.** A query is a reviewed artifact; an author chooses one and supplies parameters
**No dashboards and no exploratory analysis.** Scope §8 is explicit, and a report is not a BI tool with prose around it

**No revising the source.** A revision (DAT-057) changes what this document says, never what the source system holds. DAT-N02 is why: a connection that could write back would put this product inside somebody else's change control
**No unmarked revision.** There is no way to make a hand-entered value look like a queried one (DAT-059), and no setting that turns the marking off
**No autonomous publishing.** Nothing a model produces reaches a reader without a person accepting it
**Not a model host.** The product calls endpoints; it does not serve models
**No training on customer content.** This product does not train on it. An endpoint that does may only be used where that is stated in configuration (GEN-031)

**No tool the product does not define.** The assistant's tools are the product's own capabilities and nothing else (GEN-007) - a rule about what it may **do**, never about what a user may **ask** (GEN-047, GEN-050)
**No shared personal prompt.** A personal prompt is private until somebody promotes it (GEN-055); there is no setting that shares one, and none that lets a template bind one
**No silent discard.** A generated proposal leaves the record only by somebody discarding it deliberately, and the fact that they did stays (GEN-040, GEN-041)
**Not an identity provider.** Authentication federates to the customer's provider, or to a Google account where the tenant has none. The product holds no password (IAM-042)
**No permission finer than a component.** A component is the unit of reuse and of review; permissions inside one would have to travel with it into every document that uses it

**No sharing between tenants.** An outsider participates as a guest principal inside the host tenant (section 11), never as a bridge between two. Cross-tenant sharing is deferred rather than refused - see [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md)
**No enforcement in the renderer.** The renderer is untrusted in both deliveries; what it hides is presentation, and the service refuses regardless
**No permission outside a role** (IAM-062). A grant binds a role to a principal or a group at a level; there is no per-user permission set beside it, because section 8 could not explain one
**No vendor account inside a tenant** once it is bootstrapped (IAM-061). Support reaches a tenant through access that tenant granted, bounded and can revoke (**ADM-023**), and by no other route
**No unattended import**, at any scale (IMP-003)
**No claim of lossless Word round-tripping** (IMP-025)
**No import that bypasses validation** (IMP-017)
**No migration service disguised as a feature.** Bulk conversion of a legacy estate is a project, and it is a person's job

**No scanning of body content for personal data.** Section 4's scope is the identities a document carries as metadata and annotations. A customer's name inside the prose of a report is content the customer wrote, and this product does not inspect, classify or redact it

**No unattended import _of a foreign document_** (IMP-003, IMP-N01). The product's own export format is not a foreign document: it is already components, needs no split judgement, and is importable (IMP-039)
**No ontology with inference** (LIB-027)
**No terminology as text macros.** A term is a reference; expansion is how one is inserted, not what one becomes (LIB-019)
**No boilerplate here.** A standard phrase or paragraph is reuse, and belongs to **REU** as a component or a variable
**Not a full termbase.** Concept-level modelling, term extraction and translation memory are separate products
**One definition per term.** A term carrying two senses is two terms. Concept-level modelling is the termbase LIB-N04 rules out, and a single definition slot is the deliberate consequence

**No mirror of an external source.** The product searches PubMed, Crossref and their like and keeps what a document cites (LIB-031, LIB-033). Ingesting a registry would be maintaining somebody else's database badly
**Not an electronic signature provider.** The product records an attested act; a qualified signature is somebody else's business
**No editing or deletion of audit entries**, by anybody, including an administrator
**No workflow scripting.** Transitions are declared, not programmed; an escape hatch here becomes an unauditable path
**Not a records management system** for anything other than this product's own content
**No branching by copying.** A divergent line (LIF-044) is a declared relationship between revisions of one artifact, never a duplicate artifact somebody keeps in step by hand
**Not a version control system.** Divergence here is a regulated fact - two revisions effective in two places - not a development workflow. Nothing rebases, cherry-picks, replays or rewrites history
**Not a translation management system.** Vendor selection, quoting and translator workbenches belong to a TMS
**No translation memory of its own.** That belongs with the vendor's tooling
**No automatic publication of machine translation** (LOC-024)
**No mixed-language output by accident.** A fallback is a document-level policy and is marked in the output (LOC-037, which superseded LOC-011)

**No translating a binding.** A bound value is translated at resolution against a declared lookup, or it is not translated at all (LOC-043). Editing a resolved value inside a variant is how a document comes to disagree with its own data
**Not a prepress system.** No imposition, colour separation, trapping or bleed management

**No web publishing channel, and no anonymous distribution.** The output is documents, not a site. A report meant for the public goes on a web server, and the product's involvement ends at the file ([ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md))
**No editing of output.** A published artifact is produced from a baseline; correcting it means correcting the document and publishing again
**Google Docs is not held to the fidelity bar**, and must not be sold as though it were
**No unconstrained any-to-any relationships.** Every type is declared (scope §9 decision 8)
**No inference.** Nothing may be concluded that nobody stated. In a regulated market, "the system inferred it" is not something anybody can sign
**No relationships replacing references.** A document assembles components through its outline, not through the graph
**No unbounded traversal**, by anybody, through any surface (REL-017)

**No relationship that grants access.** An edge is an assertion about two artifacts and never widens what anybody may see: it is refused where its creator cannot read both ends (REL-035), and it is invisible to a reader who cannot (REL-019)
**No copying content to reuse it.** A reference resolves; it does not duplicate
**No overrides that live on the component.** An override belongs to one reference (REU-012)
**No inferred inclusion.** A condition axis a profile does not set excludes (REU-024)
**No conditional content in an output, hidden.** Excluded means absent, and every publication is scanned to prove it (REU-048, which superseded REU-023)

**No ambient input to resolution.** What a document resolves to is a function of its components, profile, parameters and overrides, and of nothing else - no clock, no execution order, no identity of whoever pressed the button (REU-039)
**No search across tenants**, for any purpose including support
**No index-time permission baking.** Permissions change; an index cannot be re-written every time they do (SCH-005)
**No relevance tuning per user.** Two users with the same permissions must see the same results in the same order
**Not an analytics surface.** Counting what exists is a report, not a search (**ADM**)
**No numbering stored in content.** A number is computed from an outline, a layout and a profile, and storing one makes all three unchangeable
**Sections are not reusable.** A shared section is a component; that is what components are for
**No page geometry here.** Size, margins, running heads and columns belong to the publishing layout
**No outline without a document.** A standalone tree of sections that no document owns is a template's starting outline, and belongs to **TPL**

**No bookmarks on arbitrary content.** A cross-reference targets an outline node, a caption-bearing block, a footnote or a bibliography entry (STR-026) - things that carry identity for their own reasons (**CNT-081**, **CNT-125**). A bookmark anywhere would be an identity created solely to be pointed at, and it would have to survive every edit to the sentence around it
**No per-document and no per-author overrides.** A document that needs a different look uses a different theme (CNT-N08)
**No page geometry.** Size, margins, running heads and columns belong to the publishing layout

**No stylesheet or code supplied by a tenant.** Extension is declarative, from a fixed set of properties. Arbitrary style code would be an injection surface and would make every output format a rendering engine
**Not a design tool.** A theme is configured, not drawn
**No inverting content in dark mode.** The application's chrome may go dark; the document canvas stays the theme's paper and ink, because a theme's colours were chosen for paper
**No pivot engine.** Pivoting belongs to the query (TAB-020)
**No cell formulas.** Computation belongs in the query layer; this is not a spreadsheet
**No per-document conditional formatting.** Emphasis rules live in a style (TAB-029)
**No interactive tables in published output.** Sorting and filtering a PDF is not a thing; a report is read, not queried
**No document that stays synchronised with its template.** Moving forward is a migration, taken deliberately (section 9)
**No template inheritance in the first instance.** A template that derives from another is a reasonable idea and an unreasonable amount of consequence; see TPL-Q02
**No definitions owned here that another area owns.** A template references a theme, a layout, a query set and a prompt library; it does not contain them
**Not a form builder.** A metadata schema describes a document, not a data-entry application
**No editing of history.** A version is never amended; corrections move forwards
**No branching of documents.** A variant of a report is a profile or a separate document, not a branch (**REU**)
**No automatic versioning on a timer.** A version is a positive act (CNT-070)
**Iterations are not history.** They are recovery, they are private, and they expire

questions.question: **What data residency commitments are made?** It interacts with tenant isolation, model endpoints, malware scanning and translation vendors
questions.settledBy: The first customer who asks, which in this market is early

questions.question: **Is usage metered for pricing, or only for visibility?** Metering for pricing makes every measurement a billing dispute waiting to happen
questions.settledBy: The commercial model. Settling it feeds straight back into ADM-010, ADM-011 and ADM-035: metering for pricing raises the precision each measurement needs and the time each record must survive, neither of which can be applied retrospectively

questions.question: **How much can support diagnose from metadata alone (ADM-022)?** The aspiration is most things; the practice will find the exceptions
questions.settledBy: Experience. It should be revisited after the first hundred support cases

questions.question: **Who administers a tenant before it has an administrator?** Bootstrapping needs vendor action, which ADM-N04 is uncomfortable with
questions.settledBy: A decision on onboarding, taken deliberately rather than by whoever builds signup

questions.question: **Who may close a tenant (ADM-030)?** ADM-N04 says nothing is vendor-only, but ending a contract is a commercial act and a customer cannot be the sole author of an irreversible deletion
questions.settledBy: The commercial model, taken with ADM-Q04 - the two are the same decision at opposite ends of a tenant's life

questions.question: **How long is the grace period in ADM-030, and what survives it?** A legal hold (**LIF-021**) prevents deletion regardless of retention policy, which a closing tenant has to reckon with
questions.settledBy: Legal input, taken with **LIF**. The hold question is the one that decides whether closure can ever be final

questions.question: **Should notifications, background work, and security and data protection become areas of their own?** Each is now specified as cross-cutting requirements with named owners - COL-060 to COL-062 and API-055 for notification and webhook mechanics, ADM-040 for scheduled work, ADM-041 to ADM-044 and IAM-066 for boundaries, backup and derived copies - which is the smaller move. Each could instead be an area
questions.settledBy: Whether the cross-cutting requirements hold together as the tranches are planned. An area earns its own document when its requirements stop fitting in somebody else's, and these are close to that line rather than over it

questions.question: **Which realtime transport, and is it one channel or several?** Open decision 7 in scope §10
questions.settledBy: **Settled** by a spike. One Server-Sent Events stream per open document for presence, locks and notification nudges, fanned out through Postgres `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`; model output streams on the request that asked for it. See [ADR-0018](../../decisions/0018-realtime-one-push-channel-postgres-fan-out.md)

questions.question: **How many MCP tools is the right number (API-024)?** Too few and an agent cannot do the job; too many and it does none of them well
questions.settledBy: Evaluation against real tasks, which is the only way to find out

questions.question: **Where do extensions run?** In-process is fast and dangerous; out-of-process is safe and slow, and both are a support burden
questions.settledBy: The architecture, and how much a connector is expected to do

questions.question: **Is the API public, or for integrators under contract?** It changes what deprecation costs and how much the specification must promise
questions.settledBy: A commercial decision as much as a technical one

questions.question: **Do batch create and update endpoints exist for native content?** API-N05 rules out unattended import of foreign documents; content this product already holds, moving between tenants or systems that speak its format, is a different case
questions.settledBy: The first integration that needs it. The risk of adding it early is that it becomes the bulk-import door API-N05 closed

questions.question: **Are extensions versioned and pinned per tenant (API-048)?** An extension updated under a tenant that depended on its old behaviour is the same failure as an unversioned API, one layer out
questions.settledBy: The architecture decision in API-Q03. Where extensions run largely decides whether pinning is cheap

questions.question: **What are the synchronous surface's availability and latency numbers (API-050)?** Scope §11 budgets opening, publishing, keystrokes and search, and names an availability target, but no number covers an ordinary API request
questions.settledBy: The first load testing against real content, and the commercial answer to API-Q04 - what is promised depends on who it is promised to

questions.question: **Which formats are permitted (AST-001)?** SVG in particular is a document format that can carry script, and refusing it costs real capability
questions.settledBy: A security decision: sanitise SVG on ingest, or rasterise it, or refuse it

questions.question: **Are video and audio in scope at all?** They have no place in a PDF and an obvious one in an HTML reading view
questions.settledBy: Whether HTML output becomes a real reading format

questions.question: **Where does malware scanning happen (AST-003)?** A third-party service is the usual answer and it means uploads leave the tenant boundary
questions.settledBy: A decision with **IAM**, and a customer with data residency requirements will force it

questions.question: **Does licence enforcement (AST-023) block or warn?** Blocking a publish over a metadata field somebody forgot will not be popular
questions.settledBy: Whether customers treat asset licensing as a control or as a record

questions.question: **Which classes of file are assets (AST-038)?** The purpose said "embedded objects", which is wider than anything the requirements describe, and AST-N03 rules out an attachment locker without saying where the line is
questions.settledBy: A decision taken with **AST-Q01** and **AST-Q02**, which each move it. Raster images and vector graphics are in; a spreadsheet a figure embeds, a CAD drawing, a PDF placed as a page are each a separate yes or no

questions.question: **Who renders an attribution required by a licence (AST-045)?** Recording the requirement is this area's; a credit line under a figure, in a list of illustrations, or in a colophon is a layout decision
questions.settledBy: A decision with **PUB** and **STY**. The requirement to record it does not wait on the answer

questions.question: **What is the canonical equation representation (CNT-043)?** MathML, LaTeX, or a structured form
questions.settledBy: The publishing engine decision - it constrains what can be rendered to PDF faithfully

questions.question: **Is the three-level vocabulary in section 11 adopted, and what are the interim saves called?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Adopted as iteration / version / revision in [ADR-0006](../../decisions/0006-iteration-version-revision.md); the scope, the domain package and the spike findings are reconciled

questions.question: **What exactly is the boundary that cuts a version (CNT-070)?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** A positive act only - an explicit save or a deliberate lock release. Never inactivity: a version records that somebody decided something, and time passing is not a decision. Iterations are retained until the next version, so nothing is lost when a lock times out

questions.question: **Does the mark vocabulary need an extension point?** CNT-006 closes it, which may not survive a real customer
questions.settledBy: The first customer requirement that cannot be expressed with the closed set

questions.question: **How is an authored table's cell identified for a footnote anchor (CNT-037)?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** An authored table is data too: it may declare key columns, and anchoring then works exactly as it does for a bound table (CNT-107). Positional fallback where no key is declared, marked as the weaker form

questions.question: **May a document override the theme's resolution of an image's size (CNT-088)?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled: no.** Only styles the configuration provides. An administrator adds a style; a document picks one. See CNT-N08

questions.question: **Is a forced page break content or structure?** "This section starts on a new page" reads like an outline property; "keep these two blocks together" reads like a content one. Recommendation: the first in **STR**, the second here
questions.settledBy: A decision in **STR**, since the outline is where the first half would live

questions.question: **Do style catalogues need their own capability area?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled: yes.** Added as `STY`, the eighteenth area, with scope §7.18. Style catalogues span the editor and the publisher and belonged to neither

questions.question: **How do review and authoring interact for a user who may do both?** Note what is _not_ open: suggestions with accept and reject are settled by scope decision 4 and specified in §7.7 and CNT-033. What is open is whether a reviewer who also holds authoring rights may edit directly instead of suggesting, and whether an author may suggest to themselves rather than simply typing
questions.settledBy: A decision in **COL**, informed by whether review in this market is expected to be a separate pass or a mode anyone can drop into

questions.question: **Which area owns a document being created from a template?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled: a new one.** Added as `TPL`, the nineteenth area, with scope §7.19 - template authoring, the metadata schema and structure outline definitions nothing else owned, declared parameters, instantiation, divergence, and what happens when a template changes after documents exist

questions.question: **Who owns a component's own metadata - its title, its tags?** **TPL** owns the metadata schema a document declares and **SCH** searches the values, but no area states where a component's own title and values live, or what validates them
questions.settledBy: **Half settled.** The structural half is here: CNT-142 to CNT-144 give a component its own title and close the set of attributes every component carries. The typed half is still open - a component is _typed_, and a type declaring the metadata its components carry is a subsystem the size of TPL's metadata half. What would settle it: a decision on where component types live, given that a document's schema comes from its template but a component is transcluded into many documents and so cannot take its type from any of them

questions.question: **What is the reference configuration the preview budget is measured on (CNT-136)?** Two seconds on what, rendering what content
questions.settledBy: The first performance harness, which has to name a machine before it can report a number. A budget with no baseline can be neither confirmed nor refuted

questions.question: **What happens when content carrying a condition arrives in a space whose axis does not exist (CNT-132 to CNT-135)?**
questions.settledBy: A decision in **REU**, which owns axes. Three candidates - refuse the paste, drop the condition and report it, or create the axis - and the third is how a taxonomy quietly becomes whatever anybody pasted

questions.question: **Should CNT-091 to CNT-093 be superseded by their STY equivalents?** They said what STY-016, STY-017, STY-029 and STY-030 say, and two owners of one rule is how the two drift apart
questions.settledBy: **Settled: yes.** CNT-091, CNT-092 and CNT-093 are superseded by STY-016, STY-017 and STY-029. This area keeps what content carries - a named style and no absolute dimension (CNT-121, CNT-123) - and **STY** owns how a style resolves. `docs/design/themes.md` claims the STY requirements directly

questions.question: **Is block alignment ever the author's?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Alignment comes from a named style, chosen from a catalogue - and so do paragraph, table, image and citation appearance generally (CNT-094)

questions.question: **May a reviewer who also holds authoring rights edit directly instead of suggesting?** Carried from CNT-Q10
questions.settledBy: Whether review in this market is a separate pass or a mode anybody drops into

questions.question: **What is the default lock timeout (COL-008)?** Too short interrupts thinking; too long blocks a colleague
questions.settledBy: Observed behaviour. Fifteen minutes is a guess, not a finding

questions.question: **Can a thread be private to some reviewers?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Internal threads are required, not optional, because external reviewers exist (COL-038 to COL-040). See [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md)

questions.question: **Does the soft-lock bet survive contact with users?** Scope §13 names it as a risk, and it is the one thing here that a demo will be judged on
questions.settledBy: Early evaluations. The content model stays CRDT-compatible either way

questions.question: **What are the two idle periods in COL-046 - the one after which a lock may be taken, and the one after which it releases?** COL-Q02 asks half of this question; COL-046 is why it is two
questions.settledBy: Observed behaviour, as with COL-Q02. The ordering is fixed by COL-046; the numbers are not

questions.question: **May a principal who can accept suggestions but cannot author hold a lock in order to accept one?** COL-041 makes accepting an edit, which ties it to the lock and so to authoring rights
questions.settledBy: A decision in **IAM**. If such a principal exists, either the lock admits a narrower claim or the right implies the other

questions.question: **May a block binding produce a chart as well as a table?** A declared chart in a report is ordinary in this market and is not the exploratory analysis §8 rules out - but it needs a declared chart type and encodings, resolved by a style
questions.settledBy: Whether a first customer's reports contain generated charts. If yes it is an **STY** catalogue plus a renderer, not a BI tool

questions.question: **How is "the source has moved" detected cheaply (DAT-036)?** Re-running every query to find out whether anything changed defeats the point of pinning
questions.settledBy: What connectors can actually offer - a row version, an etag, a modified timestamp - which differs by source. Whatever the answer, it is declared per connector under DAT-073 rather than assumed of all of them

questions.question: **What does a pinned value mean to a reader who cannot see the source (DAT-024)?** They see a number obtained under somebody else's access
questions.settledBy: A decision with **IAM**: whether pass-through connections may be used in documents with a wider readership

questions.question: **Do query definitions need to compose?** One query over the result of another is a common request and a common way to end up with an ETL tool nobody meant to build
questions.settledBy: A customer requirement that cannot be met by writing one query in the source

questions.question: **How much does a published document show about a revision (DAT-059, DAT-062)?** That a value was revised, or also what the query had returned and why somebody disagreed with it
questions.settledBy: A decision with **PUB**, and the first customer whose output a regulator reads. Provenance holds both halves either way; this is about what the page shows

questions.question: **What is the aggregate execution limit (DAT-071), and is it per tenant, per connection or per source?** A baseline with four hundred live bindings is one document to an author and a denial of service to a source
questions.settledBy: Measurement against a real source, and what connectors report about their own capacity. The limit exists either way; the number and its shape do not yet

questions.question: **Does accepted generated content stay marked?** Keeping the mark makes GEN-026 answerable for ever; removing it treats accepted text as authored
questions.settledBy: A regulatory view. The safer answer is to keep the record even after the mark stops showing

questions.question: **May a model see content the user can read but should not send outside the tenant?** Permission and data residency are different questions
questions.settledBy: A decision with **IAM** and **ADM**, forced by the first customer with residency rules

questions.question: **How is a prompt tested?** A prompt is a versioned artifact whose behaviour is not deterministic, which makes review hard to define
questions.settledBy: Whether prompt evaluation belongs in the product or beside it

questions.question: **Does the assistant get memory across sessions?** Useful, and a second store of customer content with its own permission problem
questions.settledBy: Whether the value survives the governance it would need

questions.question: **Who configures the guardrails (GEN-049), and how much may a tenant change?** A tenant that can weaken them has a product liability; one that cannot has a compliance department it cannot satisfy
questions.settledBy: A decision taken with the first regulated customer, and a view on what the product refuses on its own behalf rather than on a tenant's

questions.question: **Is a conversation transcript retained, and who can see it?** Distinct from GEN-Q04: that asks whether the assistant remembers, this asks whether the record survives and is discoverable
questions.settledBy: **LIF** retention, and a legal view. A transcript is customer content with a second copy of whatever it retrieved

questions.question: **Pure federation, or a first-party identity provider with federation as an option?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Federation, plus Google-authenticated accounts where a tenant has no provider yet, and never a local password. See [ADR-0009](../../decisions/0009-federation-and-google-accounts-no-local-passwords.md)

questions.question: **Is the component really the finest useful grain (IAM-N02)?** Section-level permission is asked for in regulated submissions, where one annex has a narrower readership than its report
questions.settledBy: A customer requirement that cannot be met by putting the annex in its own space

questions.question: **Is there anonymous or link-based read for a published artifact?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Link-based, never anonymous: a publication is shared to a named recipient who proves who they are once (PUB-057 to PUB-060). See [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md)

questions.question: **How does cross-tenant collaboration work, if at all?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled for now.** Guest principals inside the host tenant, and true cross-tenant sharing deferred until customers' clients become customers themselves. See [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md)

questions.question: **What happens to a guest's attribution when their access is revoked?** Their comments and accepted suggestions are part of the audited record of how the document reached its wording, and a name that vanishes from a five-year-old baseline is the failure this specification keeps finding. An erasure request points the other way
questions.settledBy: Legal advice on where attribution in an audited record sits against a right to erasure, which is a question about the regime rather than about the product

questions.question: **Is the same human guesting for three tenants three unrelated principals?** ADR-0008 implies yes, and a shared directory across tenants would be a convenience that quietly crosses the isolation boundary
questions.settledBy: Whether a guest ever needs to see their work across tenants in one place, which nobody has yet asked for

questions.question: **What makes IAM-010 and IAM-035 immediate, and what does the check cost?** Short-lived tokens with refresh, an introspection call per request, or a revocation list each buy immediacy at a different price, and the answer constrains every service the product ever has
questions.settledBy: An architecture decision, which this one owes and does not yet have. IAM-055 states the property the answer must have

questions.question: **How many days is the timetable in IAM-006 and IAM-058?**
questions.settledBy: **ADM-Q06**, which asks the same question from the administrative end. One clock, one number, one answer

questions.question: **May a tenant buy a grace window for an identity provider outage (IAM-064)?** Failing closed is correct and means an outage at the provider is an outage of the product
questions.settledBy: A customer with an availability expectation that collides with failing closed, and a view on whether that risk is theirs to accept

questions.question: **How does assisted import scale to a legacy estate of thousands?** IMP-003 forbids unattended import and a customer will have four thousand reports
questions.settledBy: **A measured number, from the first customer migration: documents converted per person per day, with IMP-031's accepted-unchanged rate beside it.** It settles before T6 is planned, because the two answers build different things - throughput work in the product (queued proposals, reviewer tooling, IMP-029), or a stated boundary saying an estate is a services project (IMP-N04)

questions.question: **Should a model propose the breakdown (IMP-004)?** It is a good use of one and it is exactly where a bad proposal is expensive
questions.settledBy: Whether the proposal is reviewed faster than the breakdown could be made by hand, measured the same way as IMP-Q01. IMP-030 means the answer changes who proposes and nothing else: the constraints on a proposal hold whatever produced it

questions.question: **Which XML vocabularies are worth importing (IMP-016)?** DITA is the obvious one and it is a large mapping
questions.settledBy: A customer with an existing structured estate. Until then it stays a `should`

questions.question: **Does export include iterations?** They are recovery rather than record, and a customer leaving may still want everything
questions.settledBy: A decision with **VER**, probably no, stated in the export

questions.question: **How far does a re-import go (IMP-036)?** Recognising the source and showing what changed is settled; reconciling a changed source against components an author has since edited is a three-way merge, and a large piece of work
questions.settledBy: A customer who re-imports rather than edits in place. Until one exists, IMP-036 recognises, shows and offers, and a person decides component by component

questions.question: **Does a term need a lifecycle of its own?** A glossary in a regulated environment is often approved, which means states and gates
questions.settledBy: Whether customers govern terminology the way they govern content. In pharma they do

questions.question: **Where does first-use expansion reset (LIB-016)?** Per document is obvious; per chapter is what several house styles actually require
questions.settledBy: Real house styles. It is a publishing-layout property if it varies

questions.question: **Do bibliographies need to be per space or shared (LIB-030)?** A shared one is maintained once and permissioned coarsely
questions.settledBy: Whether early customers' sources are confidential. In clinical work they can be

questions.question: **Should the product detect terms an author typed as text?** Suggesting a reference where somebody wrote the words is valuable and intrusive
questions.settledBy: Whether it can be offered without becoming a spell-checker that argues

questions.question: **How are record identities scoped - space, tenant or global - and does a shared library expose one identity or a view per space?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Unique within the tenant, and a share is one record seen from several spaces rather than a copy in each (LIB-041, LIB-042). Labels may collide across spaces, because a label was never the identity (LIB-043)

questions.question: **Is bibliography dedupe enforced at manual creation as well as import, and on which fields?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Both, on the same detection (LIB-044), using canonical identifiers first - DOI, PubMed identifier, ISBN, ISSN - and a declared title-author-year comparison only where none exists (LIB-045)

questions.question: **Which external sources are in the declared list (LIB-032)?** PubMed and Crossref are the obvious two for this market; registries, standards bodies and a customer's own catalogue each cost an adapter
questions.settledBy: The first customers' citation practice. The list is declared and extensible either way, so this decides the order it grows in rather than whether it can

questions.question: **Does a retracted source block a publish or warn (LIB-036)?**
questions.settledBy: Whether customers treat a retraction as a control or as a record - the same question **AST-Q04** asks about a licence, and it should get the same answer

questions.question: **Which regimes are targeted first?** 21 CFR Part 11, SOX and GxP overlap but differ in what they require of a signature and a record
questions.settledBy: The first customer. It decides how much of section 4 is needed at once

questions.question: **Is the audit log write-once at the storage layer, or only by policy?** LIF-025 says impossible through any product surface, which is weaker than immutable
questions.settledBy: The storage decision, and whether an auditor will accept application-enforced immutability

questions.question: **How does erasure of personal data work against LIF-025 (see VER-038)?**
questions.settledBy: One design decision covering both, taken with legal input

questions.question: **Do components have their own lifecycle, or only documents?** A component approved once and reused in forty reports is attractive and hard
questions.settledBy: **Settled: yes, and it is not optional.** Customers were unambiguous - an approved component carries value on its own and stays approved while the document around it is still being polished. Section 5, LIF-036 to LIF-041, with "latest approved" as a third reference mode

questions.question: **How far does bringing a divergent line back go (LIF-045)?** Choosing a side is simple and loses work; reconciling two changed revisions is a three-way merge of content, which is a large piece of work
questions.settledBy: The first customer who diverges and then converges. Until then LIF-045 requires comparison, an explicit act and a record of what was left behind, which is the part that cannot be added later

questions.question: **What happens by default when a review date passes and nobody acts (LIF-059)?** A state change is safe and disruptive; a flag is gentle and ignorable
questions.settledBy: House procedure at the first regulated customer. LIF-059 makes it declarable either way, so this decides the default rather than the capability

questions.question: **Is the scope a revision is effective for (LIF-042) the same axis as a profiling condition (**REU**)?** A plant and a market look like conditions, and effectiveness is a property of a revision rather than of content
questions.settledBy: A decision with **REU**. Sharing the axis makes one vocabulary; separating them stops a content filter deciding what is legally in force

questions.question: **Can the source language differ per component, or is it per space?** An acquired department may author in another language
questions.settledBy: Real customers. Per component is more general and complicates every status calculation

questions.question: **What granularity does translation status need (LOC-015)?** Per component is simple; per block is what avoids retranslating a page for one word
questions.settledBy: The cost of retranslation in practice, which is a commercial question

questions.question: **Do bound values get translated?** A number does not; a category name returned by a query might
questions.settledBy: **Settled: yes, at resolution, never in the variant.** A declared lookup keyed by what the source returned (LOC-043), so the binding stays inert as LOC-020 requires. Where no lookup exists the value renders as the source gave it and is reported as untranslated

questions.question: **Does a document's outline translate?** Section titles are content; the structure is not
questions.settledBy: Whether translated documents ever differ structurally, which in regulated submissions they sometimes must

questions.question: **Which languages and locales are supported at launch (LOC-038)?** The list is declared and the locale data versioned either way; what is open is which entries it starts with, and which right-to-left locale the suite runs against
questions.settledBy: The first customers' markets. A regulated submission's languages are decided by where it is filed, so this follows the first filing rather than a product preference

questions.question: **Which pagination and PDF engine?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Typst, rendering the resolved content model through one fixed template. See [ADR-0013](../../decisions/0013-typst-rendering-resolved-data-through-a-fixed-template.md)

questions.question: **Does Google Docs export survive at all?** It exists because customers ask for it and cannot express what the product is for, and it now has a second problem: writing to a user's Google Docs needs Drive scopes, which are restricted, which means app verification and a periodic security assessment - exactly what IAM-044 and [ADR-0009](../../decisions/0009-federation-and-google-accounts-no-local-passwords.md) were taken to avoid
questions.settledBy: Whether a customer wants it enough to accept both that it is visibly worse and that it carries a compliance cost nothing else in the product does

questions.question: **Is PDF/A required, and at which conformance level?** Archival and submission requirements differ by regime, and the levels are not interchangeable
questions.settledBy: The first customer with a submission requirement that names one

questions.question: **How is preview made fast enough (CNT-096) while using the same pipeline (PUB-006)?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Typst compiles incrementally, reusing unchanged layout between compiles: an edit reaches page 40 of a 300-page document in under half a second, whatever page it is on. The one difference is PUB-061. See [ADR-0013](../../decisions/0013-typst-rendering-resolved-data-through-a-fixed-template.md)

questions.question: **Can an incremental compilation be made byte-identical to a clean one (PUB-076)?** Reusing layout between compiles is what makes preview fast; producing the same bytes either way is what makes PUB-043 checkable
questions.settledBy: Measurement against the engine. If it cannot, the answer is that preview compiles incrementally and publication always compiles clean - which costs seconds on a path that already takes thirty

questions.question: **Does this need a graph store, or recursive queries over the primary one?** Open decision 6 in scope §10
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Recursive queries over the primary store, de-duplicating so a hub cannot multiply the work, with every interactive traversal capped. See [ADR-0017](../../decisions/0017-relationships-in-postgres-traversed-by-recursive-sql.md) and [`Relationship_Spike_Findings.md`](../spikes/Relationship_Spike_Findings.md)

questions.question: **How is permission filtering done without traversing what the user cannot see?** Filtering after traversal is correct and leaks timing; filtering during it is harder
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** During: the permission test is inside each recursive step, so an unreadable artifact is counted and never expanded. What traversal time still says about unreadable neighbours is a stated residual risk in [relationships.md](../../design/relationships.md)

questions.question: **Should relationships be inferable from references?** A document using a component is a relationship in everything but name, and materialising it doubles the data
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** References appear in traversal and the graph view, marked as hard dependencies, read from where they live rather than copied into the relationship table

questions.question: **Do relationships cross spaces, and may they cross tenants?** Cross-space is useful and interacts with **IAM-016**; cross-tenant is forbidden by IAM-001
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Across spaces where the user may read both ends, as references may (IAM-016); never across tenants (IAM-001, [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md))

questions.question: **Can the instances of a deprecated type be moved to its replacement (REL-037)?** Deprecation without a migration leaves a tenant maintaining two vocabularies for ever
questions.settledBy: Whether a customer deprecates a type with enough instances to make re-typing by hand unreasonable. The capability is a bulk change over edges, which REL-048 already constrains

questions.question: **Can metadata filtering (REL-051) stay inside REL-031's budget?** Filtering by type is an index; filtering by a declared metadata shape may not be
questions.settledBy: Measurement against the million-component tenant the spike used. If it cannot, metadata filtering belongs to the background report (REL-032) rather than to interactive traversal

questions.question: **Does the override mechanism actually hold (section 5)?** The spike's case 6 was never run, and it is the case where the discarded alternative is stronger
questions.settledBy: Running case 6: one component in two documents where one needs a single word different

questions.question: **May a condition apply to a whole component reference, as well as to content inside one?** "Include this section only for the regulator" is an obvious want
questions.settledBy: Whether it is expressible as an outline-node condition in **STR** instead, which may be cleaner

questions.question: **How many profiles does one document have in practice?** Two is easy; twelve makes preview, comparison and publication counts awkward
questions.settledBy: Real customer profiles. It affects whether publishing per profile is a routine act or a batch job

questions.question: **Can conditions nest or combine with logic?** "UK and not draft" is asked for the moment two axes exist
questions.settledBy: Whether simple set membership survives a real house style. Boolean conditions are easy to add and very hard to review

questions.question: **May a parameter set be declared per profile, so that variables rather than conditions carry per-profile wording?** REU-047 makes conditional alternatives the documented path; parameters would make it a table instead
questions.settledBy: Real house wording differences. Conditions suit a sentence that differs; parameters suit a value that differs, and customers will have both

questions.question: **Are full-text and semantic search one system or two?** This is open decision 5 in scope §10, and it decides how SCH-005 is implemented once or twice
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** One: both in the tenant's Postgres schema, in one query behind one interface, restricted by the same predicate and returned as one labelled list. See [ADR-0016](../../decisions/0016-search-in-postgres-behind-one-interface.md)

questions.question: **How is query-time permission filtering made fast enough?** Filtering after retrieval is correct and slow; filtering inside the index is fast and stale
questions.settledBy: **Settled** by a spike and four rules: each search planned for its own permission set, the vector strategy chosen by how much the user may see, ranking bounded, and counts capped. See [ADR-0016](../../decisions/0016-search-in-postgres-behind-one-interface.md) and [`Search_Spike_Findings.md`](../spikes/Search_Spike_Findings.md)

questions.question: **Are earlier versions searchable by default (SCH-003)?** Searching all history finds more and surfaces text that was deliberately changed
questions.settledBy: Whether customers expect superseded wording to be findable. In regulated work, sometimes emphatically not

questions.question: **Does semantic search need its own permission story?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** No, and it must not have one. Vectors sit in the tenant's schema beside the content they derive from, so the permission filter is a join evaluated before ranking rather than a post-filter over results. See [ADR-0012](../../decisions/0012-relational-version-chain-hashed-content.md)

questions.question: **Should a guest's ranking use statistics that include content they cannot see?** SCH-032 accepts that leak within a tenant, and a guest is an outsider inside it ([ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md))
questions.settledBy: Whether the difference between a guest's trust and a member's justifies ranking guests without corpus statistics. Recommended: yes, since it costs a mode of the same query and not a second system

questions.question: **How much fuzzy matching (SCH-041), and where does it stop?** An edit distance that finds a typo also finds a different word, and in a regulated corpus a near miss presented as a match is worse than nothing
questions.settledBy: Real queries against real content. The requirement is that approximation is stated where it happens; the distance itself is a number to tune

questions.question: **May a number ever be overridden by hand?** "Section 4a" appears in real submissions, usually because a numbered thing was inserted after a document was already cited elsewhere
questions.settledBy: A real regulatory submission that requires it. The default answer is no, because an override is a stored number by another name

questions.question: **Do cross-references need to cross documents?** A submission may reference a section of a companion report by number
questions.settledBy: Whether early customers submit related documents as a set. It would make resolution depend on a baseline of something else, which is a large change

questions.question: **Is an index in scope at all (STR-043)?** It needs marked entries in content, which is a CNT change
questions.settledBy: A customer whose house style requires one. Marked as `should`, not `must`, until then

questions.question: **How is "above" or "below" resolved (STR-027)?** It depends on final pagination, which the editor cannot know
questions.settledBy: The publishing engine decision, since only the paginator knows whether a target is above

questions.question: **Are catalogues tenant-wide, or per space?** A consultancy working for two clients may need two house styles that authors must not confuse
questions.settledBy: Whether early customers serve more than one end client from one tenant. Likely yes in this market

questions.question: **Does STY-N03 survive a real house style?** Declarative properties cover most of typography and none of the last five per cent somebody's brand guideline insists on
questions.settledBy: The first house style that cannot be expressed. The answer is probably to widen the declared property set rather than open an escape hatch

questions.question: **Who supplies typefaces, and who holds the licence?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled.** Product-supplied faces are open-licence only; a customer's brand face is supplied by the customer under the customer's own licence. See [ADR-0010](../../decisions/0010-open-licence-typefaces-only.md)

questions.question: **Does a theme need variants - screen against print, light against dark?**
questions.settledBy: **Settled for the editor.** No: the canvas stays paper when the application goes dark (STY-N05). Whether the HTML reading format needs a screen palette is left to its design. See [themes.md](../../design/themes.md)

questions.question: **What contrast ratio binds a customer's own brand palette (STY-069)?** A house style whose colours fail 4.5:1 is a real thing, and refusing it outright refuses the customer
questions.settledBy: Legal and commercial advice with the first brand that fails. The likely answer is that the product's own themes must pass while a tenant's are warned rather than refused, which is a different requirement from the one written today

questions.question: **How narrow can the reshaping set stay (TAB-021)?** Every customer will ask for one more transformation, and each is reasonable alone
questions.settledBy: The first request that cannot be met in the query. The answer is usually a better query

questions.question: **Does an interactive table belong in an HTML output?** A read-only PDF cannot sort; a web reading view could
questions.settledBy: Whether HTML output (PUB-056) becomes a real reading format or a convenience

questions.question: **What is the strategy for a table too wide to fit (TAB-033)?** Rotation, scaling and splitting all have bad cases
questions.settledBy: Real report shapes; wide tables of measurements are common in this market

questions.question: **Should totals ever be computed here at all (TAB-009)?** Forbidding it removes the disagreement TAB-010 exists to disclose
questions.settledBy: Whether sources can always be asked for a total. Often they can and sometimes they cannot

questions.question: **Can a document be created without a template at all?** A blank document is an obvious thing to want and an easy way to bypass every guarantee here
questions.settledBy: Whether early users need one. The likely answer is a minimal default template rather than no template

questions.question: **Do templates need to inherit (TPL-N02)?** An organisation with twelve report types that share eleven twelfths of their structure will ask
questions.settledBy: The first customer with a family of templates. It interacts badly with versioning, since a change to a parent is a change to every child

questions.question: **How much may a parameter change after instantiation (TPL-021)?** Changing the site a report is about invalidates every bound value in it
questions.settledBy: Whether re-parameterising an existing document is a real workflow or a wish. If real, it is closer to a migration than an edit

questions.question: **Does a required component (TPL-014) float or pin?** Boilerplate that updates everywhere is the point of reuse; boilerplate that changes inside an approved document is not
questions.settledBy: A decision with **VER** and **LIF** about whether an approved document may contain a floating reference at all

questions.question: **What is the default iteration retention window (VER-004)?** Too short loses work; too long is storage spent on keystrokes
questions.settledBy: Observed authoring behaviour. A day is a plausible starting guess and no more than a guess. [ADR-0012](../../decisions/0012-relational-version-chain-hashed-content.md) makes the cost concrete: the expiry sweep is cheap, the storage is not

questions.question: **How is resolved-output comparison implemented (VER-031)?** It needs two full publishing runs, or a resolved intermediate that can be diffed
questions.settledBy: The publishing engine decision, since comparing rendered PDFs is not the same as comparing what produced them

questions.question: **How is erasure reconciled with immutability (VER-038)?**
questions.settledBy: A design decision with legal input, taken once and recorded

questions.question: **Which gates take a baseline automatically (VER-021), and is that the default?** That it can happen is settled; what is open is which gates do it and whether a tenant starts with it on - every approval producing one is tidy and may also produce thousands nobody wanted
questions.settledBy: Whether lifecycle gates in practice are frequent or rare, and what the first regulated customer's gate map looks like

questions.question: **What is the similarity threshold in VER-028?** The number is tuned against one case and is the least defensible thing the spike produced, and VER-029 makes its consequence visible rather than correct
questions.settledBy: Real content, in volume. Until then a match by similarity is reported as such (VER-029), which is what stops the number being relied on silently

owns.howItIsMet: A tree of typed block nodes, JSON-serialised, validated in `packages/domain`. Read as same-family with the editor rather than object-identical - see "How CNT-001 is read"
`id` is required on every block, allocated at creation and unique within the component
A mark is a member of a set on a text node, never an element, so two marks cover overlapping ranges with nothing between them
`id` is required on every mark; an annotation fragmented across text nodes repeats one id
Resolution acts on a mark id rather than a position, so every fragment of one annotation resolves in one operation
The mark schema is a closed discriminated union. A new type is a schema version with a migration and a fixture, not a setting
No milestone, no range-start, no range-end, no standoff table. The overlap needs no construct because marks are sets
No node and no mark has a member for a typeface, a size, a colour or spacing. There is nowhere to put one
Resolution rewrites content and preserves `id` on every block it keeps
One parse entry point validates on creation, on change and on read-back. No other path constructs a document
`schemaVersion` is a member of the root, so content describes itself once it leaves the database. VER-010's column is derived from it at insert and the two must agree
A fixture directory per schema version, never deleted, and one test migrating every fixture to current
A failed read returns a named quarantine result identifying the artifact, the version and the failure. No path yields partial content
`title` is a member of the root
`title` and `language` are inside the versioned content, so they are inside `content_hash` and a version records what the component was called when it was cut
The root's members are closed - `schemaVersion`, `title`, `language`, `direction`, `content` - and the identifier belongs to the artifact. Adding a member is a schema version
`paragraph`, the default block
`list` carries `kind`: ordered, unordered or definition
A list item holds block content, so a list nests by construction and six levels is a floor rather than a limit, in any mixture of kinds
An ordered list carries `start` and `format` - decimal, alphabetic or roman - local to that list and unrelated to the outline's numbering
`table` declares header rows and header columns, carries cell spans, and carries a caption
`figure` carries an asset reference and a caption, and never asset bytes
`preformatted` holds text with whitespace significant and an optional language label
`blockquote` holds block content and an optional attribution, which may carry a citation inline
`equation` as a block
Alternative text is a three-state and absent is not one of them, so publishing cannot find it missing because it cannot be missing
There is no spacer construct, and validation refuses two adjacent empty paragraphs - see "What CNT-023 forbids, exactly"
Validation requires at least one block, and a newly created component is exactly one empty paragraph
A caption-bearing block carries the same required `id` as any other block, which is the identity the outline numbers by
Every block carries `id` whether or not it carries a caption, so any block can be a cross-reference target
A table cell holds inline content and `image` is an inline node, so an image in a cell needs no construct of its own
A figure and an inline image each carry `imageStyle`, a name drawn from the catalogue STY owns
Neither carries a width, a height or a unit of any kind. There is no member to hold one
`text` is the only leaf node, and marks apply to it
`equation` inline
`footnote` is an inline node placed at the span it annotates, carrying the note's content
`crossReference` carries a target and a display kind, and has no member for a number or a title
`citation` inline
`variable` carries a name and no value
`binding` carries a query reference and no value
Eight character marks: emphasis, strong, underline, subscript, superscript, inline code, defined term, quoted phrase
